At 1047 PM EST, a Weatherflow station at Dog Bar Breakwater measured a convective gust to 64 mph, in association with a fine line of showers and isolated thunderstorms.

At 1232 AM EST, a Weatherflow site at Deer Island recorded a gust to 59 mph.  This was due to strong post-frontal wind gusts -- not in association with a convective line that moved through a few hours prior.
At 1016 PM EST, a Weatherflow site at Hatch Beach in Eastham recorded a wind gust to 59 mph.  This was well ahead of a convective fine line that moved through an hour or so later.
At 1149 PM on March 7, a Weatherflow station atop Mt. Tom recorded a post-frontal wind gust to 72 mph.
At 1214 AM EST on the 8th, the ASOS at Logan International Airport (KBOS) recorded a post-frontal wind gust to 58 mph.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Nantucket (KACK) recorded sustained wind speeds of 40 mph.  No damage was reported.

Several large limbs were downed on East Mountain Road.  At the same time, a broadcast meteorologist estimated that wind speeds were around 60 mph.

Large branches and a transformer near Cold Spring Road were downed by thunderstorm winds resulting in brief power outages.  In addition, several utility poles along Graniteville Road were blown down, resulting in the closure of that road at its intersection with Main Street.

At 345 AM EDT (245 AM EST), a Weatherflow mesonet site at West Island recorded a wind gust to 66 mph.  At 458 AM EDT (358 AM EST), a Weatherflow station at The Knubble at Horseneck Beach in Westport recorded a wind gust to 69 mph.  At 459 AM EDT (359 AM EST), the ASOS at the New Bedford Airport (KBED) recorded a gust to 52 mph.  The following reports were from law enforcement, relayed via amateur radio operators. They all occurred between 413 AM and 628 AM EDT (313 AM and 528 AM EST).  In Westport, multiple small branches were down on the entire length of Old Harbor Road; power lines were down on Pine Hill Road; and a tree and wires were down on Tickle Road.  In Somerset, a tree and power lines were down on Hargraves Avenue.  In New Bedford, a tree was down on Reed Road at Stonewall Avenue; a large tree branch was down on Acushnet Avenue; and a tree and wires were down on a car on Bullard Street.  In Fall River, a large tree was down on the southbound lane of Plymouth Avenue; the fire department reported a tree down on wires on an unspecified street.

In Falmouth at 615 AM EDT (515 AM EST), a trained spotter reported a gust to 57 mph. In Chatham at 513 AM EST, the ASOS at the Chatham Airport (KCQX) recorded a gust to 56 mph. In Provincetown at 522 AM EST, the AWOS at the Provincetown Airport recorded at gust to 56 mph.  In Barnstable at 229 AM EST, the Fire Dept. reported wires down on Main Street.  In Orleans at 354 AM EST, police reported a large limb down on Route 6A.  In Sandwich, between 447 AM EST and 500 AM EST, law enforcement reported a large tree down on Service Road at Tarragon Drive and a tree down on Great Hilll Road near Popple Bottom Road.  In Brewster at 504 AM EST, the Fire Dept. reported a tree down on a detached garage on Gages Way.  In Dennis at 514 AM EST, law enforcement reported a large branch down on Old Chatham Road at Kelley Way.  In Falmouth at 523 AM EST, police reported a large tree down on a house's service wires, but no street name was given.  All of the aforementioned reports were relayed by amateur radio operators.

Winds generally were gusting to 55 to 60 mph.  In Mattapoisett at 526 AM EDT (426 AM EST), a tree was down on wires on Old Brandt Island Road, per law enforcement relayed by amateur radio.  In Rochester at 626 AM EDT (526 AM EST), amateur radio operators reported a tree down on Negus Way, a tree down on Clapp Road between Deerfield Terrace and Marys Pond Road, and a tree down on Burgess Avenue.

Winds generally were gusting to around 55 mph.  The ASOS at Plymouth recorded a gust to 55 mph and a spotter in Falmouth recorded a gust to 57 mph.  In Lakeville at 502 AM EDT (402 AM EST), high tension power lines were down on Pickens Street near Precinct Street.  In Middleborough between 556 AM EDT (456 AM EST) and 621 AM EDT (521 AM EST), law enforcement reported a tree and wires down on Fuller Street and a tree down on Marion Road between Stony Point Road and Long Point Road.  In Hanson, a tree was down on Camp Kiwanee Road.

Winds generally were gusting to around 50 mph.  In Boston at 454 AM EDT (354 AM EST), the ASOS at Logan International Airport (KBOS) recorded a gust to 46 mph.  In Boston at 359 AM EDT (259 AM EST), police reported a tree down on a car on Camden Street (relayed by amateur radio).

Winds generally were gusting to around 50 mph.  In Peabody at 452 AM EDT (352 AM EST), a tree was down on Forest Street.  In Gloucester at 602 AM EDT (502 AM EST), a tree was down on Washington Street.  In Lynn at 630 AM EDT (530 AM EST), a tree was down on Commercial Street.  The aforementioned reports were from law enforcement, relayed by amateur radio operators.
Winds generally were gusting to 40 to 50 mph.  In Natick at 504 AM EDT (404 AM EST), the fire department reported a tree down on Beaver Dam Road at Mill Street.
At 458 AM EDT (358 AM EST), the ASOS at the Nantucket Airport (KACK) recorded a wind gust to 62 mph.  No damage was reported on the island.

In Narragansett at Point Judith, a Weatherflow mesonet station recorded a wind gust to 79 mph at 450 AM EDT (350 AM EST).  In Narragansett at 503 AM EDT (403 AM EST), the fire department reported a utility pole and wires down on Sand Hill Cove Road...and at 515 AM EDT (415 AM EST) police reported a large tree down on cable wires on Austin Street.

In Providence, 7 to 10 inches of rain fell over the course of a few hours during the mid to late afternoon creating serious flash flooding. 8.31 inches of rain fell in the Elmwood section of the city and 6.89 in the College Hill section.  National news media showed aerial views of Interstate 95 which had become completely flooded and was closed in both directions. The snarled traffic lasted for multiple hours. Cars were reported to be stuck in the following locations: Webster Ave., Hamilton St., Cadillac Ave. at Melrose St. (water up to the windows), Narragansett Ave at Santiago St., Rugby St. at Thurbers Ave. Additional flooding and road closure reports included: Thackery St. at Melrose St., the underpass of Rt. 10 north at Westminster St., Hartford Ave. at Heath St., Smith St. at Gentian Ave., Exchange St., Pleasant Valley Parkway at Berlin St., Huntington Ave., Manton Ave. at Saban St., Elmwood Ave. ramp to Rt. 10, and Olneyville Square.  One block of Atwells Avenue was washed out. Many water rescues were necessary due to life-threatening situations.  All together, there were 3 injuries related to motor vehicle accidents during the storm and roughly 25 individuals rescued.  On Benevolent St. water invaded the 1st floor of a Brown University campus building. On Elmwood Ave. there was rapid flooding of a structure of unspecified type.  On Peace Street, there was a partial (25%) collapse of the roof of a vacant building, which was being redeveloped into a shopping plaza.  A total of 41 homes and businesses were flooded.  The West River overtopped its banks and flooded Charles Street and portions of Silver Spring Street in the evening.  The Woonasquatucket River crested at 6.07 ft. at 315 AM on September 7th, which was above the 5.5 ft. flood stage.  Many thanks to the Providence Emergency Management Agency for some of these details.

Snowfall totals included 6.9 inches in Ashburnham (Co-Op Observer), 6.0 inches in Sterling (Trained Spotter), and 5.5 inches in Princeton (Public).

In the higher terrain of far northwest Middlesex County, 5 to 7 inches of snow fell.  In Pepperell, a trained spotter reported 6.3 inches.  Other reports included 8.0 in Ashby (which may have been too high) and 5.4 inches in Tyngsboro - just to the east of MA Zone 26.
Five to six inches of snow fell in western Essex County.  Snowfall totals, from trained spotters, included 5.8 inches in Methuen, 5.5 inches in Haverhill, and 5.2 inches in North Andover.

In Revere, at Noon EST, Mills Avenue and Archer Avenue were closed due to coastal flooding.  In the Dorchester section of Boston, from 1212 PM to 1218 PM, both lanes of Morrissey Blvd were closed from between Freeport Street and the University of Massachusetts, as well as the ramp from I-93 to Morrissey Blvd., due to coastal flooding.

In Quincy at 1218 PM EST, a car was stuck in coastal flooding on East Squantum Street at Victory Road.  Victory Road was flooded and impassable.
In Salem at 1215 PM EST, several streets were reportedly closed due to coastal flooding.  In Ipswich at 120 PM EST, Jeffrey's Neck Road was flooded and impassable.

Snowfall amounts ranged from 6 to 11 inches in the higher terrain in western Franklin County.  In Hawley, a Co-Op observer reported 11.4 inches.  In both Rowe and Leyden, reports of 6 inches were received.  In Buckland, police reported a tree down on Mohawk Trail (Route 2), blocking both lanes.  The report was relayed by amateur radio.

In Chatham at 115 AM EST, a mesonet site recorded a wind gust of 57 mph.  At Hatch Beach in Eastham at 112 AM EST, a mesonet site recorded a wind gust of 54 mph.  In Orleans at 116 AM EST, police reported a tree down on Monument Road.  In Barnstable at 5 AM EST, police reported a tree down, damaging a car near the intersection of Old Colony Road and Gosnold Street.
In Freetown at 146 AM EST, Fire Dept. officials reported a tree and wires down near Howland Road.  Winds generally were gusting to 45 to 50 mph in southern Bristol County.

The Vineyard Gazette and GoMV.Com showed photos of moderate flooding in Vineyard Haven on Water Street near the Steamship Authority and in the Five Corners area.  In Edgartown, moderate coastal flooding also occurred, with the Dock Street flooded (via the Chappaquiddick Ferry) and other flooding on the Chappaquiddick side of the harbor.  In Oak Bluffs, the was moderate flooding on Lake Avenue and Beach Road, per the Vineyard Gazette and Martha's Vineyard Times.

Minor to moderate flooding occurred on Nantucket, per photos from Massachusetts Coastal Zone Management.  Coastal flooding occurred on New Whale Street, Harbor View Way, Easy Street, Easton Street, and Oak Street.
In Quincy, portions of East Squantum Street, Dorchester Street, and the causeway near Victory Road were flooded.
Winds generally were gusting to 40 to 50 mph.  In Groton at 6 AM EST, a tree was down on Route 119 a the Littleton town line.

Winds generally were gusting to 45 to 55 mph.  A gust to 55 mph was recorded on the ASOS at Norwood Airport (KOWD) at 351 PM EST.  In Foxboro, at 830 AM, a tree and wires were down on the corner of Pleasant Street and Mechanic Street.  In the evening, a tree and wires were down on Walnut Street, a tree was down on a Dassance Drive, and a tree was down on Main Street.

Winds generally were gusting to 50 to 60 mph.  In Plymouth, to the east, a wind gust to 62 mph was observed at 921 PM EST.  In Middleboro at 850 AM EST, a tree was down on power lines on Chestnut Street.  In Whitman at 805 PM EST, a large tree was down on a house on Harvey Lane.  In Halifax at 850 PM EST, a tree was down on a vehicle and a house on River Street and on nearby Summit Street wires were down.

In Upton at 950 AM EST, a tree was down on wires near James Road.  In Auburn at 4 PM EST, a tree was down on Hill Street.  In Sturbridge at 615 PM EST, a tree was down on Dennison Drive.  In Charlton at 630 PM EST, a tree was down on A. F. Putnam Road at Willow Tree Lane.  In Worcester at 7 PM EST, a large tree was down on a house on Indian Lake Parkway and at 740 PM EST, a tree was down on wires and cars on Mallard Road and Austin Street.  In Grafton at 8 PM EST, a tree was down on a house on Sartell Road.

Winds generally were gusting to 45 to 55 mph.  In Boxford at 950 AM EST, a large tree was down on power lines on Topsfield Road at Cedar Street.  In Andover at 1106 AM EST, a tree and wires were down on Argilla Road at Newman Hill Drive.

Winds generally were gusting to 40 to 50 mph.  In Weston at 10 AM EST, a large tree was down on Chadwick Road near Chestnut Street.  In Westford at 1215 PM EST, a large tree and power lines were down on Acton Road.  In Sherborn at 647 PM EST, a tree and power lines were down on South Main Street at Sawin Street.

Winds were generally gusting to 50 to 60 mph, but at the highest elevations, a mesonet site atop Mt. Tom recorded a gust to 78 mph at 617 PM EST.  In Southwick at 1230 PM EST, a tree fell onto a SUV on Feeding Hills Road (Route 57), which sadly killed a 6-month old passenger.

Winds generally were gusting to 45 to 65 mph on Cape Cod.  In Dennis at 945 PM EST, a CoCoRaHS observer recorded a wind gust to 65 mph.  Earlier, at 549 PM EST, a mesonet site at West Falmouth recorded a gust to 63 mph.
Winds generally were gusting to 40 to 50 mph.  In Huntington at 357 PM EST, utility poles and wires were down on Route 66.
Winds generally were gusting to 40 to 50 mph.  In Brookline at 520 PM EST, a tree was down near the intersection of Walnut and Dudley Streets.

Winds generally were gusting to 50 to 60 mph.  At 737 PM EST, the ASOS at New Bedford Airport (KEWB) recorded a gust to 54 mph.  In Freetown at 545 PM EST, a tree was down on Route 24, causing damage to the front window of a bus.  In New Bedford at 546 PM EST, power lines were down on Wood Street near Baylies Street...and at 806 PM EST a tree was down on a house near Adams Street.  In Fall River at 836 PM EST, multiple trees were down.  In Westport at 915 PM EST, a tree was down on Cummings Lane at Horseneck Road and a large tree was down on Tickle Road.

Winds generally were gusting to 50 to 55 mph.  In Mansfield at 605 PM EST, a tree was down on power lines on Ware Street between Erin Drive and Short Street.  In North Attleboro at 710 PM EST, scaffolding set up outside a building on South Washington Street fell over... and at 9 PM EST, a large tree was down on wires and a utility pole was snapped on Route 152 at Westchester Drive.
At 704 PM EST, the ASOS at Nantucket Airport (KACK) recorded a gust to 60 mph.  At 652 PM EST, a Weatherflow mesonet station at Nantucket Harbor recorded a gust to 59 mph.

Winds generally were gusting to 50 to 60 mph.  In Rochester at 855 PM EST, multiple trees were down on North Avenue at Benson Road and a tree and power lines were down near Bennett Road.  In Mattapoisett at 937 PM EST, a tree was down on Prospect Road.
Winds generally were gusting to 45 to 60 mph.  A trained spotter in far southeastern Plymouth County recorded a wind gust to 62 mph at 921 PM EST.
At 1242 PM EST, a Weatherflow mesonet station at Block Island Jetty recorded a wind gust to 60 mph.

Winds generally were gusting to 50 to 55 mph.  In Cranston at 550 PM EST, a large tree was down on Phenix Avenue and Phenix Ridge Drive.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS EAST OF IPSWICH BAY AND THE STELLWAGEN BANK NATIONAL MARINE SANCTUARY
events.event_narrative: At 1040 AM, Buoy 44018, 10 miles NNE of Provincetown, recorded a gust to 56 mph.
A Weatherflow mesonet station at the Knubble on Horseneck Beach recorded a wind gust to 57 mph at 856 AM EST.
Snow total ranged from 4 to 8.5 inches in southwestern Franklin County.  The highest reported total was 8.5 inches in Ashfield, MA.
Six to eight inches of snow fell in western Hampshire County.  Some totals included 8.0 inches in Plainfield; 7.5 inches in Chesterfield; 7.5 inches in Westhampton; and 6.2 inches in Williamsburg.
Snowfall totals ranged from approximately 6 to 8.5 inches in western Hampden County.  The highest report -- 8.5 inches -- was from Chester.

Snowfall amounts in eastern Hampshire County were highly variable, with the greatest amounts west of the Connecticut River and the lowest amounts farther east, toward Worcester County.  Some totals included: 6.8 inches in Southampton; 6.6 inches in Easthampton; and 6.0 inches in Northampton.  Farther east, 4.5 inches was reported in Belchertown and 4.0 inches in Amherst.

Snowfall amounts in eastern Hampden County ranged from 5.0 to 7.5 inches.  Some specific totals included:  7.5 inches in West Springfield; 7.1 inches in Chicopee; 7.0 inches in Agawam, Holyoke, and Southwick; 6.7 inches in Westfield; 6.0 inches in Wilbraham; 5.5 inches in Longmeadow; and 5.0 inches in Monson.

In southern Worcester County, generally 5 to 6 inches of snow fell, with the highest amounts near the Connecticut border.  Some specific totals included:  6.1 inches in Sturbridge; 6.0 inches in Southbridge; 5.5 inches at Buffumville Lake in Charlton; and 5.5 inches in Webster;l and 4.3 inches in Auburn.

Hartford County generally received 4 to 8 inches of snow.  Some specific amounts included:  8.0 inches in Granby; 7.0 inches in both North Canton and Simsbury; 6.8 inches in Bristol; 6.5 inches in East Windsor; 6.2 inches in Newington; 6.0 inches in Glastonbury; 5.9 inches a Bradley International Airport in Windsor Locks; 5.0 inches in Marlborough; and 4.0 inches in Wethersfield.

Snowfall generally ranged from 5.0 to 7.5 inches in Tolland County.  Some specific totals included:  7.5 inches in Rockville; 7.0 inches in both Coventry and Storrs; 6.8 inches in Columbia; 6.4 inches in Hebron; 6.0 inches in Andover, Bolton, and Staffordville; and 5.4 inches in Vernon.

Snowfall totals ranged from 4.5 to 6.8 inches in Windham County.  Some specific amounts included:  6.8 inches in Moosup; 6.7 inches in Eastford; 6.6 inches in Scotland; 6.5 inches in Canterbury, Hampton, and Pomfret; 6.3 inches at the Willimantic Airport; 5.0 inches in Danielson; and 4.5 inches in East Killingly.

Snowfall in northwest Providence County generally ranged from 5.5 to 7.0 inches, with the highest amounts in the higher terrain.  Some specific amounts included: 7.0 inches in Foster; 6.3 inches in Glocester; 6.0 inches in Burrillville; and 5.5 inches in Smithfield.
Snowfall generally ranged from 6 to 8 inches in western Kent County.  Some specific amounts included 8.3 inches in West Greenwich and 6.3 inches in West Warwick.
Snowfall totals in eastern Kent County included:  5.7 inches in East Greenwich and 5.2 inches at T.F. Green Airport in Warwick.  A CoCoRaHS observer 3 miles NNE of Warwick reported 4.5 inches.

Snowfall totals in Washington County generally ranged from 5 to 8 inches.  Some specific amounts included:  8.1 inches in South Kingstown; 7.5 inches in both North Kingstown and Richmond; 6.0 inches in both Charlestown and Exeter; and 5.4 inches in Westerly.

Snowfall amounts in Newport County ranged from 4.0 to 6.5 inches.  Some specific amounts included:  6.5 inches in Portsmouth; 6.2 inches in Little Compton; 6.0 inches at the Newport Airport; 5.0 inches in both Middletown and Tiverton; and 4.0 inches in Jamestown.
At 444 AM EST, the ASOS and Nantucket Airport (KACK) recorded a wind gust to 59 mph.

In Acushnet at 320 PM EST, a large tree was down on power lines near the intersection of Main Street and Heritage Road.  Winds generally were gusting to 50 to 55 mph along the south coast of Massachusetts.
At 830 AM EST, a NWS employee noticed flooding on webcam video at the Chappaquiddick Ferry in Edgartown and at Five Corners in Vineyard Haven.

Snowfall totals ranged from 8 to 12 inches in western Franklin County.  Some specific amounts included 12.1 inches in Ashfield, 11.8 inches in Rowe, 11.0 inches in Hawley, 9.5 inches in Buckland, 9.3 inches in Colrain, 9.0 inches in both Shelburne and Leyden, and 8.0 inches in Conway.

Snowfall amounts averaged 5.5 to 6.0 inches in eastern Franklin County.  Some specific totals included 7.0 inches in Montague, 5.8 inches in Greenfield, 5.4 inches in Leverett, 5.0 inches in Bernardston, 4.5 inches in both Sunderland and Shutesbury, and 4.4 inches in New Salem.

Generally, six to nine inches of snow fell in northern Worcester County.  Some specific totals included 9.3 inches in Ashburnham, 8.7 inches in Westminster, 8.4 inches in Royalston, 8.1 inches in Lunenburg, 7.6 inches in Paxton, 7.1 inches at the Fitchburg Airport, 6.2 inches in Ashburnham, 6.0 inches in Charlton, East Brookfield, and Leicester, and 5.8 inches in Princeton.
Some snowfall totals from northwest Middlesex County included 8.4 inches in Ashby, 7.5 inches in Pepperell, and 7.0 inches in Townsend.
Marginal heavy snow amounts of 5.5 inches in Methuen and 6.0 inches in Haverhill were reported.
Snowfall totals in western Hampshire County included 8.6 inches in Plainfield and 8.0 inches in Westhampton.

Snowfall in eastern Hampshire County ranged from 5 to 8 inches west of the Connecticut River to 3 to 5 inches east of the Connecticut River.  Some specific amounts included 7.8 inches in Southampton, 7.0 inches in Northampton, 5.1 inches in Easthampton, 4.5 inches in South Hadley, and 3.0 inches in Amherst.

Snowfall totals generally ranged from 7 to 8 inches in western Hampden County.  In Chester, 8.0 inches was reported by an amateur radio operator.  In neighboring Westfield (MA Zone 11), 7.2 inches was reported by a CoCoRaHS observer.

Snowfall totals varied widely from as much as 18 in the northwest hills of Hartford county to as little as 1.5 inches in the southeast section of the county.  Some specific totals include - 18.0 in Granby/Hartland, 12.5 in Burlington, 7.2 Suffield, 5.1 in Bristol, 4.5 at Bradley International Airport in Windsor Locks, 3.0 in Glastonbury and 1.5 in Manchester.  In East Hartland, at 220 pm on the 14th, multiple trees and powerlines were down with several roads impassable.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS EAST OF IPSWICH BAY AND THE STELLWAGEN BANK NATIONAL MARINE SANCTUARY
events.event_narrative: At 12:10 am on 3/15/23, buoy 44018 reported a wind gust to 58 mph.

Snowfall amounts ranged from 24 to 37 in western Franklin County.  Some specific amounts include 37.0 in Hawley, 36.0 in both Colrain and Rowe, 31.0 in Buckland, 26.0 in Ashfield, and 24.2 in Conway.  In Conway at 554 am on the 14th, trees and wires were down on Route 116.  In Rowe at 724 am on the 14th, multiple trees were down on Zoar Rd.  In Buckland at 806 am on the 14th, a tree was down on power lines on Bray Rd.  In Charlemont at 1001 am on the 14th, a tree was down on Route 2.

Snowfall amounts varied widely across eastern Franklin County from as much as 26 inches in the highest elevations to 4-8 inches in the valley.  Some specific amounts include, 26.0 in Wendell, 24.0 in Shutesbury, 16.8 in New Salem, 7.2 in Bernardston, 7.1 in Greenfield, and 6.2 in Montague.  In Northfield at 426 am on the 14th, a tree fell onto a house and cars on Millers Falls Rd.  In Greenfield at 448 am, multiple trees were down, including Country Club Rd and Birch St. at Silver St.  In Bernardston at 453 am, a tree was down on River St.  In Deerfield at 522 am, a tree was down on Hoosac Rd.  In Shutesbury at 840 am, a tree was down on wires on Cooleyville Rd.  In Montague at 9 am, a tree and power lines were down on Taylor Hill Rd. at Old Sunderland Rd.  In Greenfield at 915 am, a tree and wires were down on Bernardston Rd. (Route 5).

Snowfall amounts varied widely from as high as 24 to 32 in the highest elevations to as little as 7 in the lower elevations.  Specific amounts included 32.0 in Ashburnham, 31.5 in Royalston, 29.5 in Hubbardston, 29.3 in Princeton, 25.5 in Lunenburg, 24.0 in Gardner, 23.0 in Leominster, 19.0 in Phillpston, 17.2 in Barre, 7.2 in Warren.  In Rutland at 356 am on the 14th, a tree was down on Brigham Rd.  In Fitchburg at 415 am, multiple large trees were down on Kimball Rd, Lancaster Ave, and the Great Wolf Lodge Drive. Also in Fitchburg, at 1003 am, trees and limbs were down on Route 2. In Barre at 445 am, a tree was down on South St.  In Gardner at 740 am, a tree was down on a car on Elm St. and at noon multiple trees and limbs were reported down throughout the town.  In Winchendon at 1105 am, a tree and wires were down near School St. and Robbins Rd.; a tree was down on West St. and Irwin Ct.; and a large tree was down on wires on Hale St.  In Ashburnham at noon, two trees and wires were down on Route 12--one of the trees fell onto a car.  In Lunenburg at 110 PM, a large tree was down on power lines at Highland Street and Holdman Street; a tree was down on Graham Street; a tree was down on Cushing Lane; and a tree and wires were down on Island Road.  In Westminster at 2 PM, a tree was down on South Ashburnham Road and a tree and wires were down on Potato Hill Road.  In Leominster between 330 PM and 4 PM, an 18-inch diameter tree was down on Weathervane Drive at Currier and Ives Drive; a large tree was down on power lines on Smith Street; a tree was down on Pleasant Street near Lisa Drive; a tree was down on Tolman Avenue at Industrial Road; and a tree and wires were down on Nashua Street and Mechanic Street.

Snowfall amounts were highly variable across western Middlesex County, ranging from just over a foot in northern sections to only an inch or two in southeastern sections, where it was mainly rain.  Some specific totals included 12.9 inches in Tyngsboro, 8.7 inches in Littleton, 6.5 inches in Chelmsford, 6.2 inches in Lowell, 5.2 inches in Maynard, 5.0 inches in Billerica, 3.5 inches in Sudbury, 1.7 inches in Framingham, and 0.7 inches in Natick.  In Tyngsboro at 1005 AM, scattered trees and tree limbs were down, due to the weight of the heavy, wet snow.

Three to eight inches of snow fell in western Essex County.  Some specific totals included 8.0 inches in Haverhill, 7.0 inches in Methuen, 5.3 inches in Amesbury, 4.5 inches in both Andover and North Andover, and 3.0 inches in Boxford.  In Methuen at 243 PM on the 14th, multiple trees were down in a resident's yard on Bentley Circle.

Very heavy snow ranging from 15 to 30 inches fell in northwest Middlesex County.  Some specific amounts included 30.0 inches in Ashby and 14.9 inches in Pepperell, both from trained spotters.  In Ashby at 1030 AM on the 14th, Fire Dept. officials reported a large tree down on Rindge Road; multiple trees and wires down on Mason Road, Greenville Road near Foster Road, an Fitchburg State Road. The report was relayed by amateur radio.  In Townsend at 1130 AM on the 14th, a tree was down on Route 13 near Elm Circle; multiple trees and wires were down on Brookline Street and Fitchburg Road; a large tree was down on Meadow Road and Brookline Street; trees and wires were down on Linden Street.

Snowfall totals ranged from 32 inches in the highest terrain to about 11 inches closer to the Connecticut River valley.  Some specific amounts included:  32.0 inches in Plainfield, 31.0 inches in Chesterfield, 22.0 inches in Goshen, 12.5 inches in Williamsburg, and 11.0 inches in Westhampton.

Snowfall amounts ranged from 16 to 32 inches in western Hampden County.  Some specific amounts included:  32.0 inches in Blandford, 29.0 inches in Chester, and 16.0 inches in Granville.  In Blandford at 523 AM on the 14th, a tree was down on Russell Stage Road.

Generally, 4 to 8 inches of snow occurred in eastern Hampshire County.  Some specific amounts include 8.3 inches in Easthampton, 4.2 inches in Northampton, 3.7 inches in Amherst, and 3.5 inches in South Hadley.  In Pelham at 440 AM on the 14th, a tree and power lines were down on Gulf Road.  In Northampton at 453 AM on the 14th, a large tree branch was down on South Street and at 610 AM, a tree was down on wires on River Road.  In Hadley at 829 AM on the 14th, Mountain Road was impassable due to downed trees and power lines in multiple locations and at 903 AM trees and wires were down on Moody Bridge Road near South Maple Street.

Generally, 4.5 to 9 inches of snow fell in eastern Hampden County.  Some specific amounts included:  9.1 inches in Westfield, 8.0 inches in Southwick, 6.0 inches in Ludlow, 4.5 inches in both Springfield and West Springfield, and 4.4 inches in both Agawam and Hampden.  In Holyoke at 512 AM on the 14th, a tree was down on Rock Valley Road.  In Westfield at 545 AM on the 14th, a tree was down on Court Street.  In Southwick at 837 AM on the 14th, three power lines were down on Sheep Pasture Road; a tree was down on Klaus Anderson Road; on Wood Street, a tree fell through the roof of a house and penetrated all the way down to the basement; power lines were down on Vining Hill Road an a cross-arm was snapped.

Snowfall amounts in southern Worcester County were highly variable, with more than a foot at the higher elevations and barely an inch or two near the CT and RI border, where it was largely mixed with rain.  Some specific totals included: 14.4 inches at the Worcester Airport, 8.5 inches in Auburn, 5.2 inches in Westborough, 4.7 inches in Northborough, 2.0 inches in Milford, and 0.9 inches in Douglas.

A strong thunderstorm produced 3.37 inches of rain in Longmeadow and 2.51 inches in Springfield, per an amateur radio spotter.  In Longmeadow at 545 PM EDT (445 PM EST), the Fire Dept. reported the area of Hazardville Road and Shaker Road flooded and impassable, with a car stalled in the street flooding.  Also, on Dwight Road, two cars were stuck in street flooding.  Reports were relayed via amateur radio.  There was a report of basement flooding on Kenmore Drive in Longmeadow.  In East Longmeadow at 545 PM EDT (445 PM EST), a trained spotter reported significant street flooding, up to the wheel wells of cars, on North Main Street.
In Westport, police reported a tree down on Briggs Road, caused by a lightning strike.  Report relayed by amateur radio.
A member of the public reported on social media that hail up to quarter size occurred in Westerly, along with frequent lightning.  Report was relayed by amateur radio.
In Cambridge, Vassar Street, near MIT, was flooded and impassable per campus law enforcement.  Report relayed via amateur radio.
The public reported 0.75 inch diameter hail in South Coventry.

At 4 PM EDT (3 PM EST), the public reported quarter size hail in East Killingly.  Report relayed by the media.  At 403 PM EDT, an amateur radio spotter relayed photos of golf ball size hail from East Killingly.

Lightning caused a massive 6-alarm fire that destroyed a 160-year old church in Spencer, MA.  The steeple of the First Congregational United Church came crashing down and this made national news.  The rest of the building was destroyed.  A detailed analysis of lightning strike data showed that one strike a little north of the church occurred at 2:24:47 PM EDT but a closer one occurred at 2:29:16 PM EDT.  That was most likely the one that caused the blaze.  No injuries were reported.  Damage figure is estimated.
At 457 PM EDT (357 PM EST), a relative of a NWS employee, on Brandywine Rd. in Medway, MA, reported 0.75 inch diameter hail.

In Stow between 329 PM EDT and 333 PM EDT, there were trees down into a house on Barton Road.  A few houses down, several trees were blocking the road and one tree struck a chimney and caused it to collapse.
In Stow, a lightning strike caused a shed fire on Great Road.
At 322 PM EDT (222 PM EST), quarter size hail was reported by a NWS employee traveling on the Mass Pike in Charlton.
In Rehoboth at 439 PM EDT (339 PM EST), there was a social media photo of hail that ranged from dime to quarter size.  The report time was radar-estimated.
In New Bedford at 505 PM EDT (405 PM EST), amateur radio operators reported nickel size hail.
In Dartmouth at 518 PM EDT (418 PM EST), police reported nickel size hail.  Report relayed by amateur radio.
In Pelham on Amherst Road, the Fire Dept. reported an individual struck by lightning, with a reported foot injury.  Report relayed by amateur radio.

In Webster at 411 PM EDT (311 PM EST), lightning caused a house fire on Colonial Road. Subsequent follow-up with the fire department revealed that there was $100,000 in water damage to the home from extinguishing the fire.
In Stafford, CT near the Monson, MA border, quarter size hail was reported, per amateur radio.
In Woodstock at 438 PM EDT (338 PM EST), a trained spotter reported nickel size hail.
In Lawrence at 511 PM EDT (411 PM EST), a house was struck by lightning, causing damage to the electrical system.
In Amherst at 410 PM EDT (310 PM EST), a large tree branch and wires were down on Sunderland Road.
In the western part of Whately, a tree was down near the intersection of Haydenville Road and Webber Road.  Time estimated by radar.
In East Leverett, trees and wires were down on Shutesbury Road.  Time estimated by radar.
In Gill, a tree was down on Main Road.  Time estimated from radar.
In Northfield, trees were down on Warwick Road and Strowbridge Road.  Time estimated from radar.
In Hingham, a tree was down on Avalon Drive.
In Cohasset, the public reported trees and multiple wires down on unspecified streets. |Report relayed by amateur radio.
At 610 PM EDT (510 PM EST), a Weatherflow Mesonet station XJUD at Point Judith recorded a gust to 49 mph.
At 735 PM EDT (635 PM EST), a Weatherflow mesonet site XHUL at the Hull Yacht Club recorded a gust to 47 mph.
At 721 PM EDT (621 PM EST), a Weatherflow mesonet site XWHL at Woods Hole, measured a wind gust to 45 mph.
In Hopkinton, a house on Highview Avenue was struck by lightning, reportedly causing a small fire, which was quickly extinguished.
Flooding caused a small mudslide on Route 110, blocking the road.
In Westford, a lightning strike caused damage to the side of a house on River Street.
In Granville, a tree was down on wires on North Lane.
In Russell, a tree was down on Blandford Road.
In Mansfield, lightning caused a house fire on Hickory Lane.
In Medway, lightning started a house fire on Holliston Street.
In Franklin, lightning started a house fire on Prospect Street.
In North Chelmsford, dime size hail was reported.
In Foster, there were several reports of dime size hail.
In Millis, a tree was down on Acorn Street at Village Street.
In Medway, a tree was down on Village Street at Neelon Lane.  A tree and power lines were down on Awl Street.  Power lines were down on High Street.

In North Chelmsford at 445 PM EDT (345 PM EST), Middlesex Street at Cedar Street was closed due to flooding. At 446 PM EDT, significant street flooding was reported on Old Westford Road behind the police station, per police department...relayed by amateur radio.
In New Bedford, a tree was down on Route 140 Northbound near Exit 7 (Brayley Road).
In Dartmouth, a large tree was down on Hathaway Road at Slocum Road.
In Hingham, a tree was down on Whiting Street.
In Mashpee at 840 PM EDT (740 PM EST), a large tree and wires were down on Meetinghouse Road at Great Neck Road North.
In Falmouth at 845 PM EDT (745 PM EST),  a tree was down on Round Pond Drive and wires were down on Crooked Meadow Road.
In Portsmouth, a house was hit by lightning on Slocum Road, causing a basement fire. Report relayed by amateur radio.
In Richmond, a tree and wires were down at the intersection of Kenyon Hill Trail and Switch Road.
In Foster, a tree was down on the 100 block of Danielson Pike.
In Glocester, a tree was down on the 300 block of Cooper Road.
In Burrillville, a large tree was down on Buck Hill Road near the fire tower.  Report relayed by amateur radio.
In Princeton, trees and wires were down on Sterling Road near Town Farm Road.
A mesonet site at Block Island Jetty recorded a thunderstorm wind gust to 34 knots at 448 AM EDT (348 AM EST).
In Burlington, a tree and wires were down on Route 4 between Rt 179 and River Rd in Farmington.
In Charlemont, multiple trees were down on Route 2.
In Cummington, numerous trees were down on West Cummington Road.
In Shelburne Falls, two trees were down on Hog Hollow Road.
In Agawam, a tree was down on Pine Street.
In Templeton, a large tree was down on power lines on Barre Road near Dudley Road.
In Charlton, a tree was down on wires on Oxbow Road.  Another tree was down on Old Worcester Road.

Shortly after midnight (EDT), a microburst occurred in a section of Framingham. There was a narrow swath of about a dozen downed trees, mainly in backyards, from Kara Ann Drive eastward across Harrington Road and onto Cynthia Road.  A few of the trees were uprooted.  One tree fell onto a car in a driveway.  A window was blown out of one garage.  This was most likely a microburst, but there is a non-zero chance that this could have been a tornado.  Radar imagery and damage photos were inconclusive.
In Tewksbury, a lightning strike started a house fire on the 20 block of Sheridan Lane.
In Westhampton, a lightning strike caused a garage fire at a residence on Tipping Rock Road.  Report relayed by amateur radio.

A NWS survey determined at an EF-0 tornado, with maximum estimated peak wind of 80 mph, touched down in North Brookfield at 1056 AM EDT.  There were no injuries or damage to homes in the area.  There were several eyewitnesses to the tornado, although none of them saw an actual funnel.  One eyewitness was in an auto body shop and reported strong winds making the garage door bow inward.  Another eyewitness, the Fire Chief of North Brookfield, saw debris lofted into the air.  A third eyewitness described chaotic swirling as the tornado passed by.  The tornado is estimated to have touched down a little east of the North Brookfield Waste Water Center.  It traveled about 2 miles to the northeast, although not on the ground continuously, and ended a little east of the intersection of Ryan Road and Hillsville Road.  The damage was limited to trees, with the most concentrated damage area along Ryan Road, slightly north of the Ward Street intersection.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Worcester Regional Airport (KORH) recorded a wind gust of 68 mph.  Damage around Worcester was substantial.  St. John's Cemetary was closed after 30 to 40 trees two and a half to three feet in diameter were downed by thunderstorm winds.  In the midst of this there were also a number of gravestones that were knocked over or damaged in some other way.  Other trees in the cemetary had their tops sheared off or were completely stripped of leaves.  Numerous trees were downed across the city of Worcester.  A garage door was blown out of a building on Pleasant Street and wind blown debris shattered several of the windows of a Sovereign Bank Branch.  Four inch diameter branches were downed by these winds at the Worcester Polytechnic Institute.  In addition, trees were downed in Leicester.  Much of the damage information included here was taken from local newspaper articles.  The newspaper didn't identify a specific time when the damage occurred; however, it is assumed from radar observations and ASOS observations that the bulk of the damage occurred around the time of this 68 mph wind gust.

Tornado confirmed to have touched down in a small neighborhood in|Foxboro near the Mansfield town line very close to the town of Easton. |Several locations on a west to east path in the neighborhood had several|large trees up to 2 feet in diameter snapped at the trunk.|Observed tree damage had a convergent pattern consistent with|violently rotating winds. No major damage to homes was observed,|but one chimney appeared to have been knocked over by a fallen|tree. Path width was estimated to be around 25 yards. Path length|of the surveyed damage points was just shy of 300 yards. Per|radar data, a velocity couplet was over the surveyed neighborhood|for only a minute or two before continuing east over conservation|land. It is possible that the tornado was on the ground for|longer, but surveyors were unable to access conservation land|east of the last surveyed damage point. Additional significant |tree damage was found east of aforementioned conservation land in Easton, |but patterns were more consistent with west to east straight line winds. |This is also consistent with archived KBOX radar which displayed strong|outbound (west to east) velocities over this area.

A small EF-1 tornado touched down in the town of Mattapoisett Massachusetts|at 11:20 AM EDT. The storm was on the ground for approximately 3 minutes.|The storm moved to the northeast at approximately 20 MPH and lifted off the|ground on North Street just north of Eldorado Drive. Numerous large Pine and |Maple trees were uprooted falling in serveral directions. There were also |numerous pine trees along the path that were snapped off between 10 and 20|feet above the ground. The most concentrated damage was found along Eldorado|Drive by Granada Court. The top wind speed was estimated to be 95 mph.

A small EF-0 tornado touched down in the town of Barnstable, near|the village of Marstons Mills, at 11:52 AM. The storm tracked ENE|from Evergreen Drive for approximately four minutes before |lifting over Joe Thompson Road, at approximately 11:56 AM. The |primary damage indicators were an uprooted hardwood tree and a|downed electrical pole, supplemented by strewn debris inclusive |of smaller trees, fence posts, and branches. The damage was most |concentrated near the center of the track at the intersection of |Race Lane and Osterville-West Barnstable Road. Witnesses described|a chaotic event, observing airborne fence posts and branches. Top wind speeds were estimated at 80 mph.

A tornado caused damage in the town of Scotland, located in|Windham County, CT. The tornado touched down on Bass Road and continued along Route 14 (Huntington Road) and crossed Pinch Street before it eventually|lifted near Brook Road. While there wasn't much in the way of structural damage observed, other than gutter damage to two homes, there was significant tree|damage. A tornado caused significant damage along a discontinuous path|in Scituate, Johnston, and North Providence, Rhode Island. This |is the strongest tornado to have struck Rhode Island since the F-2|tornado in Cranston and Providence on August 7, 1986.||The tornado first touched down near Byron Randall Road in Scituate|which is where the most severe damage occurred. There were hundreds|of large trees either uprooted or snapped at their bases. One |home sustained damage to its roof, the top of its chimney was |blown off, windows were blown in, and an exterior door was |dislodged from its framing. Damage was consistent with winds of |around 115 mph which is classified as EF-2 on the Enhanced Fujita|Scale.||The tornado then tracked into Johnston where it crossed I-295 at |Exit 10 and lifted a vehicle into the air before dropping it back |onto the highway. The driver was transported to an area hospital |with minor injuries. From there, the tornado moved across Bridle |Way and Carriage Way where a number of trees were snapped or |uprooted, some of which fell onto homes or vehicles. Some homes |also lost some singles from their roofs. A metal Stop sign pole |was bent in half and the sign was blown away. The tornado then |caused damage in Highland Memorial Park Cemetery where a number of|large trees were either snapped or uprooted. The damage observed |in Johnston was consistent with winds of 90 to 100 mph which is |classified as EF-1 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale.||Finally, the tornado crossed into North Providence. Similar to|Johnston, a number of trees were either snapped or uprooted, some|falling onto homes or vehicles. Most of the damage observed was to|the north of Mineral Spring Avenue. One of the harder hit areas  |included Lydia Avenue, Armand Drive, and Bennett Street where two|homes were made uninhabitable from fallen trees. The damage |observed in North Providence was consistent with winds of 90 to |100 mph which is classified as EF-1 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale.||The National Weather Service would like to thank the Rhode Island|Emergency Management Agency, the Scituate Police Department, the|Johnston Police Department, the North Providence Fire Department,|and Skywarn Amateur Radio Operators for their assistance with the|damage survey.

An EF-1 with maximum winds of 100 mph began east of North Central|State Airport along Wellington Road in the town of Lincoln, RI. A|video did show a funnel cloud passing over the adjacent airport|but found no damage. The tornado uprooted a large tree and damaged|am estimated 20' by 30' section of roof on a building across the|street and due north of the uprooted tree. Video provided by|Lincoln Animal Control showed a thin tornado passing at the end of|the facility's driveway and twisting a large branch from a tree.|The tornado moved northeast into a field of solar panels which|uplifted two sections. From here, the tornado likely lifted before|moving across Route 146 at Route 116 which was documented on a DOT|camera. This damage and the tree damage along the path was |consistent with wind speeds between 90 and 100 mph, resulting an |EF-1 rating on the Enhanced Fujita Scale.

A National Weather Service Damage Survey Team concluded that an EF-1 Tornado occurred in a portion of Eastern Rhode Island and Southeast Massachusetts.  A waterspout occurred just off of Rumstick Point in Barrington, Rhode Island.  This waterspout then moved onto land over the southern portion of Warren near the Warren/Bristol line at Hanley Farm Road.  It then continued eastward across the Kickemuit River in the Touisset Highlands section of Warren.  It then crossed the Cole River and continued into southeastern Massachusetts.||Most of the damage had a rating of EF0 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale with wind speeds of 65 to 75 mph.  However, there was one small section of Warren in the Laurel Park area that demonstrated EF1 damage.  This was located near the intersection of Route 136 and Harris Avenue, including Overhill Road.  Wind speeds in that area were estimated at 90 mph. ||The tornado path length was 4.2 miles and for the most part was continuous.  It was very narrow with a path width of only 40 yards.  The tornado was first observed on land in Rhode Island at 4:05PM EDT.  It moved into Massachusetts around 4:09PM EDT.||No injuries were reported.  The majority of the damage was to trees, some of which fell onto power lines and houses.  There were numerous eyewitness accounts of dark funnels, swirling debris, and intense roaring.  A garage door bowed out towards the path of the tornado in one location.  A large tree near Harris Avenue was lifted up and thrown 40 feet onto Route 136.  At that location, small trailers also had been blown onto Route 136.

Several large trees and branches were blown down on the south side of Fearing Pond in Myles Standish State Forest.  Eyewitnesses reported waves up to two and a half feet tall formed on the small pond.  The strong winds from the northwest hit a steep embankment and a thick stand of pine trees 35 to 50 feet tall.  This resulted in a couple of small kayaks on the beach on the southeast corner of the pond being lifted up and blown ten to fifteen feet.  Numerous tents on the southside of the pond also were blown about 20 to 30 feet.  Numerous trees were blown down in the area of New Grassy Pond, a kettle pond that sits at the base of a bowl in the terrain.  Most of the damage occurred on the south side of the pond, though there were a couple of trees blown down on the north side of the pond.  The trees on the north side of the pond were downed from the winds circling around the edge of the bowl that the pond is sitting in.  This also resulted in the water in the pond being pushed out approximately two feet beyond the normal water line around the majority of the pond.  The only other damage consisted of some shingles being blown off a small cottage on the south side of Fearing Pond and a camping trailer on the southeast side of the pond that had two holes punctured in the roof from falling tree limbs.
Golfball to lime sized hail fell in the Cedarville section of Plymouth.
Some vehicle damage occurred with quarter sized hail that fell in Wellfleet.

A reliable observer measured a wind gust of 80 mph in Falmouth.  At the Hyannis Airport ASOS (KHYA) blizzard conditions were reported between 520 AM EST and 530 PM EST. Cape Cod suffered nearly total power outage for a time, and power outages stretched well into the middle and end of the week.

At the New Bedford Airport ASOS (KBED) blizzard conditions occurred from 745 AM EST to 400 PM EST. The highest gust was 62 mph at 748 AM EST. New Bedford MA (EWB) observations are not available after 1000 am due to ASOS failure, so end time is estimated. Generally 26-33 inches of snow fell. The highest amount was 37 inches in Bliss Corner.

At the Norwood Airport ASOS (KOWD) blizzard conditions occurred from 520 AM EST to 1255 PM EST. The highest gust was 58 mph at 555 AM EST. Generally 18-24 inches of snow fell. The highest amount was 32.5 inches in Sharon.

This was a very disruptive storm with travel nearly impossible at the height of the storm. In Providence, plows were ordered to stop for a time as it was impossible to safely plow.

Thunderstorm wind damage began about half a mile north of Lake Street on the west side of New Bedford Reservoir in Acushnet.  Damage extended to the south-southeast ending at the intersection of Main Street and Perry Hill Road.  Numerous trees were either blown over or snapped at a level between 8 and 14 feet above the ground.  Near Athol Street, a concentration of white pines were snapped off approximately 15 feet off the ground.  These trees ranged in diameter from 12 to 20 inches.  Three houses were damaged by trees falling on them.  On the west side of Main Street just to the northwest of the golf course, numerous oak trees were blown over or had large branches blown off.  Also, numerous white pine trees standing between 30 and 45 feet tall were blown over or snapped off between 12 and 20 feet above the ground.  Numerous power lines were also downed.  A mile long section of North Main Street was closed because almost every utility pole was damaged.  Leonard and Lake Streets were also closed because of downed trees and power lines.Based on the amount of tree damage and the good health and size of the trees it was estimated that windspeeds reached 80 to 100 mph.  Damage was determined to be the result of straight line winds most likely associated with a microburst.

A National Weather Service Damage Survey Team determined that a waterspout occurred in Apponagansett Bay.  The waterspout produced damage in two locations roughly two miles apart and was approximately 25 yards wide.  It travelled north to south even though the parent thunderstorm was moving to the northeast.  The waterspout appears to have originated near the Apponagansett River shore at the end of Day Street and travelled about 30 yards.  It moved over the water weakening as it moved down Apponagansett Bay and over the Padanaram Bridge.  It produced a second area of damage south of the bridge around 100 yards long.  Seven boats were overturned and at least partially sunk by the waterspout off of Bayview Avenue.  The waterspout was close enough to shore that strong inflow winds resulted in the downing of three trees right on the shore line and minor damage to a property at the end of Day Street.

Heavy rainfall associated with Tropical Storm Hanna ranged from 2.60 inches to 5.95 inches in Tolland County.  This resulted in several basements flooding and a washout on Summer Street created a sinkhole.

Heavy rainfall associated with Tropical Storm Hanna resulted in 4.79 inches to 6.56 inches of rain across Hillsborough County with Manchester receiving 4.79 inches.  Most of this rain fell between 6pm EDT and midnight which resulted in flash flooding across Manchester.  Numerous streets and basements were flooded with up to two feet of water: including Bridge, Beach, Central, and Chestnut Streets.  The police department garage was flooded with six feet of water and buckled an asphalt ramp that leads into the garage, making it unusable.  The floodwaters then ran into the firing range, gym, an office and an electrical system, causing the police station to have to use backup power from the fire department next door.  At least two police cars ended up with significant water damage.  All told the police station sustained at least $100,000 in damage.  The fire department used a rescue boat to rescue seven to ten people from submerged cars and one from a flooded home.  The Manchester Library's basement auditorium and a nearby room was flooded with up to six inches of water.  The worst flooding occurred in the Crosbie Street neighborhood where three houses were uninhabitable for several days and 13 others were damaged.

Heavy rain associated with Tropical Storm Hanna ranged from 4.69 inches to 6.18 inches in western Hillsborough County.  This resulted in flooding.  In Goffstown, a thirty foot section of road washed out.
Heavy rain associated with Tropical Storm Hanna ranged from three to four inches resulting in flooding of Waterman and Edmond Streets.
Heavy rain associated with Tropical Storm Hanna ranged from four to five inches resulting in street flooding that closed several streets.

Heavy rain associated with Tropical Storm Hanna ranged from two to three inchees.  This resulted in flooding on Endicott and Walnut Streets and Railroad Avenue with two to three feet of water.  At least one car was stuck in the flood waters.

Heavy rain associated with Tropical Storm Hanna ranged from three and a half to five and a half inches.  This resulted in widespread street flooding across central Hampden County.  The Union Street underpass in West Springfield was flooded.  In Wilbraham, multiple roads were flooded, including Main Street and several locations on Route 20 and Route 32.  Minor mudslides occurred on Route 32.  Both Holyoke and Springfield experienced widespread street flooding.  Route 32 and several other roads were rendered impassable by floodwaters in Monson.  Several vehicles on these roads became disabled.  In addition, three residences were flooded along a retention road.

Heavy rain associated with Tropical Storm Hanna ranged from three and a half inches to six and a half inches.  This resulted in widespread street flooding.  Following are a few of the reports.  A one hundred foot section of Stonybrook Road in Milford was washed out.  Multiple cars were stuck in flood waters under the railroad bridge on Cambridge Street in Worcester.  Extensive flooding occurred on Cambridge Street with water up to ten feet at one business. A stream in Westborough extended its banks blocking off a portion of Warren Street.

Heavy rain associated with Tropical Storm Hanna ranged from 2.28 inches to 3.64 inches.  This resulted in flooding of the Woburn Police Department garage.  Newspapers reported that as many as ten vehicles were towed from flood waters on Route 9 under the 126 overpass.  This is a frequent problem in Framingham when it rains.
Heavy rain associated with Tropical Storm Hanna resulted in the Quinebaug River overrunning its banks, flooding low lying areas.
Heavy rain associated with Tropical Storm Hanna resulted in the Quinebaug River overrunning its banks, flooding low lying areas.
A second batch of heavy rain associated with Tropical Storm Hanna resulted in widespread street flooding.  A portion of Route 3 Southbound and a few other roads were closed due to the flooding.
Lightning from an embedded thunderstorm associated with Tropical Storm Hanna struck a house on North Pleasant Street resulting in a fire.

Three and a half to five and a half inches of rain fell across Bristol County as tropical moisture streamed northward from Hurricane Kyle.|In Somerset, this heavy rainfall resulted in Buffington Brook exceeding its banks and two feet of water running over County and Buffington Streets.  Several businesses sandbagged their property.  A large sinkhole formed on County Street.  A car was stuck in flood waters on Brayton Avenue and two people had to be rescued by boat.  The Lees river overran its banks at Main Street in Swansea, resulting in flooding of Main Street.  President Avenue and Pierce and Doval Streets in Fall River were also flooded with at least two feet of water.  At least two cars were stuck in flood waters and manhole covers popped off in other locations.  In addition, several basements were flooded.

Four to six inches of rain fell in New Bedford with tropical moisture streaming northward from Hurricane Kyle.  This resulted in street flooding.  County Street was closed due to three feet of water on the road.  The intersection of Purchase Street and Coggeshall, as well as Hillman Street also were flooded.

An Onset mobile home park was flooded with two and a half feet of water.  One mobile home was moved off its foundation by these flood waters.  Also, East Boulevard in the Onset section of Wareham was closed due to flooding.

Heavy rainfall behind Tropical Storm Kyle resulted in flash flooding across Hartford.  On Elliot Street and on Flatbush Avenue, a total of six cars were stuck in flood waters.  Numerous basements were flooded on both Maple and Wethersfield Avenues and on Parkview Drive.

Tropical Storm Hanna made landfall near the North Carolina/South Carolina border at 320AM EDT September 6.  Hanna then moved north/northeast across the Mid-Atlantic states and southern New England September 6 and 7.  Storm total rainfall in southeast Providence County ranged from four to five inches.  The highest sustained wind of 25 knots (29 mph) and gust of 35 knots (40 mph) were recorded at T.F. Green Providence Airport.  The lowest sea level pressure was 996.0 mb at T.F. Green Providence Airport.  A coastal storm surge of 2 feet above normal tide was experienced at Providence, RI.  No coastal flooding was reported.  Several trees, wires, and a transformer were blown down in southeastern Providence County.  All of the associated effects of Hanna in southeastern Providence County resulted in no loss of life or injuries, and $13K in property damage, all from wind.

Tropical Storm Hanna made landfall near the North Carolina/South Carolina border at 320AM EDT September 6.  Hanna then moved north/northeast across the Mid-Atlantic states and southern New England September 6 and 7.  Storm total rainfall in southern Bristol County ranged from two to three inches.  The highest sustained wind of 24 knots (28 mph) and gust of 33 knots (38 mph) were recorded at New Bedford Regional Airport.  The lowest sea level pressure was 995.4 mb at New Bedford Regional Airport.  Several trees and wires were blown down in southern Bristol County.  A boat in New Bedford Harbor was blown off its mooring as well.  All of the associated effects of Hanna in southern Bristol County resulted in no loss of life or injuries, and $3K in property damage, all wind related.

Tropical Storm Hanna made landfall near the North Carolina/South Carolina border at 320AM EDT September 6. Storm total rainfall in southern Plymouth County ranged from two and a half to a little over four inches.  The nearest Automated Surface Observing Station at Plymouth Municipal Airport measured a sustained wind of 18 knots (21 mph) and a gust of 36 knots (41 mph).  The lowest sea level pressure was 995.6 mb at Plymouth Municipal Airport.  Several trees and wires were blown down in southern Plymouth County.  All of the associated effects of Hanna in southern Plymouth County resulted in no loss of life or injuries, and $7K in property damage, all attributed to winds.

Two feet of water was over the road near Route 18, rerouting cars.  Also, a small brook overflowed its banks, flooding a backyard.

Several trees were downed throughout southern Bristol County, including in Seekonk, New Bedford, and Dartmouth.  Two of these trees were blocking roads, while the other two landed on cars when they fell.

A utility pole and a tree were downed by strong winds.  The tree fell, blocking a road.  The Automated Surface Observing Station at Plymouth Municipal Airport (KPYM) recorded 31 mph sustained winds with at least one gust to 45 mph.

Minor coastal flooding occurred in Wellfleet, where a car got stuck in water moving over Lieutenant Island Road.

A narrow tornado moved through Wethersfield.  The NWS storm survey team found damage beginning near the intersection of Nott Street and Park Avenue and continuing southeast into a cornfield along Elm Street, between Maple Street and Interstate 91.  ||Along this track, numerous trees were downed.  One of these trees fell onto a car on Park Avenue, trapping a person.  Another fallen tree blocked the exit ramp of Exit 24  on Interstate 91.  Many of these trees were large, healthy oak trees that were sliced in half, sheared off at their bases, or uprooted.  One tree fell onto a house with such force it split the house in half.  Two of the residents were inside the house at the time, but escaped without injury.  One injury indirectly occurred as a result of this tornado, when a split branch high up in a tree fell the following day, striking a person.||In the cornfield at the end of the tornado track, cornstalks were found flattened in a criss-cross pattern.  Farther into the cornfield, cornstalks were found to have not been impacted at all by the winds.  ||At a sporting goods store along the tornado track, a kayak inside the store was sucked out onto the road through a front window.

Three firefighters were treated for heat exhaustion and dehydration while fighting the fire.  One was transported to the hospital.  These injuries were indirectly related to the lightning strike.

Portions of Route 18, Acushnet and Wamsutta Streets, and numerous other streets in New Bedford were closed due to flooding.  In Dartmouth, two to two and a half feet of water inundated the area near Longfellow Street and Lexington Avenue.

A 41 year old man was out digging for quahogs (clams) on the tidal flats of Little Pleasant Bay, a quarter mile east of Sipsons Island when he was struck by lightning and killed.

Numerous roads were flooded and subsequently closed as anywhere from two to four inches of rain fell across Middlesex County.  The most affected areas include Framingham and Marlborough.  In Framingham, roads were closed due to mudslides as well as flooding, including Routes 126 and 9.  Walking trails at Garden in the Woods were also washed out.  In Marlborough, basements were flooded and a portion of the driveway at the New Hope Community Church was washed out.

Numerous roads were flooded and subsequently closed across much of southern Worcester County.  The worst flooding was experienced in Westborough and Worcester.  The Westborough News reported it as the worst flooding Westborough has seen in years.  The Westborough fire department took 57 calls due to either flooded basements or motorists stranded in flood waters.  Flooding was especially bad in the streets behind Westborough High School, south of the Westborough Reservoir and around the Jackstraw Brook.  In Worcester, numerous streets were flooded and washed out.  Two people were rescued from flood waters in Southborough.  In addition, a couple of propane tanks had to be secured at a house on Parkerville Road because they were floating in the waters.  The Southborough Fire Department received 26 calls of basement flooding.  Six inches of water inundated the Southborough Public Library's children's section, damaging books.
Penny to golf ball size hail fell in Hopkinton.  So much hail fell that two hours after the storm moved out of the area, hail was still piled three inches deep in numerous locations.

Nine people, taking shelter under a tree at Foster Memorial Park, were injured when lightning struck nearby.  Five of the injured refused medical treatment, the other four were transported to a nearby hospital.  There were only minor injuries.  No information was available on their ages.
Lightning struck a house on North Lane, resulting in a house fire.

In Hancock, a house on Middle Road had a flooded basement with the furnace under water.  In Petersborough, two basements were flooded on 7th and Union Streets.  Also, City Avenue was flooded and impassable.

A little over five inches of rain fell in eight hours, with most of the rain falling between 3 and 7pm across Hillsborough County.  This resulted in numerous road closures.  Two of these roads were closed as the result of a mudslide and collapsed hillside that spread across the Route 202 North just before its intersection with Route 136 in Peterborough.  In addition, portions of Routes 136 and 101, as well as Ashlee Drive and Sand Hill, Old Dublin, Slab, Gulf, Old Greenfield, Forest, Cavender, County, Old Bennington and Hopkins Roads were undermined, flooded, and/or closed.  The Peterborough Fire Department rescued seven people who were trapped in their cars on Old Greenfield Road.  Route 101 east flooded with two to three inches of flowing water, which flooded and eroded yards nearby.  Floodwaters were forceful enough that they moved a guardrail on Route 136.

Dublin and Harkness Roads were both flooded, resulting in road washouts on both.  Dublin Road was able to be re-opened two days later.  Harkness Road was completely washed out and remained closed several days later.  In addition, at least one basement was flooded in Jaffrey on Pine Street.

Minor coastal flooding occurred in Narragansett at Scarborough Beach and in Charlestown.  Ocean waters reached the base of the boardwalk at Scarborough Beach.  In Charlestown, several driveways on Charlestown Beach Road were flooded with ocean waters.
High surf flooded Galilee Beach in Narragansett up to the dunes with significant beach erosion occurring.

On the southwestern coast of Nantucket, in Madaket, three homes on Massachusetts Avenue were surrounded by ocean waters.  Only one of the homes is occupied and water two and a half feet deep surrounded that home.
Two people were trapped on top of their car after driving into flood waters in an underpass near the intersection of South and West Streets.

Stafford Square in Fall River was flooded with water two and a half feet deep and the westbound lane of Roebson Street was flooded.
The intersection of Green and Bridge Streets was flooded over the sidewalks in Fairhaven.  Portions of Cranberry Highway were flooded with six to eight inches of water, rendering it impassable.

National Weather Service Automated Surface Observing System (ASOS) anemometers are typically located 33 feet above ground level.

Six inches of rain fell in less than three hours over portions of Cape Cod and southern Plymouth County.  Bourne and southern Plymouth were most affected by this with numerous roadways flooded.  Route 130 in Bourne was flooded with eight inches of water while St. Margaret's Street was inundated with three feet of water.  Buzzard's Bay Drive was flooded, as were several basements and businesses along the street.  Several cars became disabled after becoming stuck in flood waters on roadways in Onset (a village of Bourne).  Two feet of water inundated a Pleasantwood Road in Sandwich.  A portion of Lake Avenue in Wareham was washed out.  A section of Bournedale Road was washed out.  In Plymouth, numerous roads were flooded, including Lunns Way, Pond, Nameloc, Raymond, and Hedges Pond Roads, Windward Lane, and South Wind Drive.  Two cars were stuck in flood waters on Pond Road.

There were two lightning strikes at Camp Cachalot, a boy scout camp run by the Narragansett Council.  One of them struck near the dining hall where one of the|Scouts was leaning on a metal serving table.  He received a slight shock and, as a cautionary measure, the rescue squad was contacted.  One of the troop leaders accompanied the boy to the hospital where they were met by the parents - he was checked out, found to be OK, and released.
The Carson Beach Weatherflow measuring station recorded a wind gust of 41 mph.
The Automated Surface Observing Station at Logan International Airport (KBOS) recorded a wind gust of 44 mph.  No damage was reported.
The Revere Beach Weatherflow measuring station recorded a wind gust of 43 mph.
The Deer Island Weatherflow measuring station recorded a wind gust of 45 mph.
The Dread Ledge Weatherflow measuring station recorded a wind gust of 40 mph.
The Rose Island Weatherflow measuring station recorded a wind gust of 41 mph.
The Horseshoe Shoals Weatherflow station recorded a wind gust of 43 mph.
The Weatherflow reporting station at West Falmouth recorded a wind gust of 52 mph.  No damage was reported.

In Haverhill, a tree and wires were downed onto a car.

Based on damage reports in the area, occasional gusts to 58 mph are believed to have occurred throughout coastal Bristol County.  Some of these reports include: large branches and trees down in Fairhaven, Westport, Somerset, New Bedford, and Fall River.

The Automated Surface Observing Station at Blue Hill Observatory and Science Center in Milton, MA (KMQE) recorded a sustained wind speed of 39 mph with gusts to 53 mph.  Based on damage reports in the area, occasional gusts to 58 mph are believed to have occurred throughout eastern Norfolk County.  Some of these reports include: trees down in Hingham.

The Automated Surface Observing Station at Hanscom Field in Bedford, MA (KBED) recorded sustained wind speeds of 37 mph and gusts to 48 mph.  Reports of damage include: tree limbs down in Marlboro and a tree that fell on a house in Ashland.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Worcester Regional Airport (KORH) recorded sustained wind speeds of 35 mph and gusts to 47 mph.  A tree was blown down in Southboro, blocking Route 9 West and Interstate 495.

The Automated Weather Observing System at the Cape Cod Coast Guard Air Station (KFMH) recorded sustained winds to 31 mph.  In addition, spotters across Barnstable county reported wind gusts up to 60 mph.  Reports of damage included: large branches downed in Sandwich and Falmouth and trees down in Bourne and Sandwich.

The Automated Surface Observing System at New Bedford Regional Airport (KEWB) recorded sustained wind speeds up to 32 mph and gusts to 47 mph.  In addition, the Narragansett Bay PORTS system at Fall River recorded sustained wind speeds to 35 mph and a wind gust to 56 mph.  Reports of damage include: large branches and trees downed in New Bedford, Somerset, Westport, Fairhaven, and Dartmouth.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Plymouth Municipal Airport (KPYM) recorded sustained wind speeds of 32 mph with gusts to 46 mph.  In addition, spotters reported wind gusts up to 58 mph.  Trees in Duxbury were downed by these winds.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Blue Hill Observatory and Science Center in Milton, MA (KMQE) recorded sustained wind speeds to 37 mph and gusts up to 52 mph.  Reports of damage include: large tree limbs down in Hingham and a tree down in Braintree.
The Automated Surface Observing System at Logan International Airport (KBOS) recorded sustained wind speeds up to 36 mph and gusts to 47 mph.  Several reports of trees and limbs downed were received.

A 10 year old boy was killed when a birch tree was blown over by a strong gust of wind.  Photos of the tree shown on local news outlets as well as reports in local newspapers indicated that the tree was at least partially rotted.  ||The closest observations are available eight to nine miles away at either Lawrence Municipal Airport (KLWM), MA and Nashua, Boire Field (KASH), NH.  Observations on the hour either side of the accident recorded wind gusts to 43 mph at KLWM and 21 mph at KASH.
Trees were downed in Yarmouth, Barnstable, Mashpee, and Bourne.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Nantucket Memorial Airport (KACK) recorded sustained wind speeds of 41 mph and gusts to 54 mph.  In addition, a twelve inch diameter tree was downed, blocking Atlantic Avenue.
Portions of both Winthrop Parkway and Winthrop Shore Drive were flooded with ocean waters and debris.  A nearby secondary road was closed due to the amount of debris in the roadway.

A parking lot at Scituate Harbor was flooded with six to twelve inches of ocean water.  Medium size rocks from the sea were washed into the parking lot.  Lighthouse Road was flooded with six inches of water and splashover blocked access to Lighthouse Point.  Water splashing over the sea wall was reported to be hitting the roofs of nearby homes.  In addition, the parking lot for Burts Restaurant on Route 3A in Plymouth was flooded with water splashing over the sea wall.
Seaview Avenue from Oak Bluffs to Harthaven were flooded with water and debris splashing over the seawall.

Washington and Lafayette Streets were flooded with six inches of seawater.  Several streets near Brant Point were flooded as well.  The parking lots at Jetty Beach and Children's Beach also were flooded.

Numerous trees in Plymouth were downed.  Some of these trees landed on wires, one on a car.  No injuries were reported.  Trees were also downed in Scituate and Marshfield.  One of the trees downed in Marshfield landed on wires, which put enough pressure on the utility pole that it came down too.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Barnes Municipal Airport (KBAF) recorded sustained wind speeds of 35 mph and wind gusts to 48 mph.  In addition, trees were downed in Ludlow, blocking a road.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Fitchburg Municipal Airport (KFIT) recorded wind speeds of 36 mph and gusts to 52 mph.  In addition, trees were downed on Pleasant Street in Leominster and large branches were downed on Clarendon Street in Fitchburg.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Hanscom Field in Bedford, MA (KBED) recorded wind speeds to 35 mph and wind gusts of 46 mph.  In addition, a tree and wires were downed on Hancock Street in North Reading.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Norwood Memorial Airport (KOWD) recorded wind speeds to 31 mph and gusts to 46 mph.  In addition, a tree and wires were downed on Crescent Circle in Holbrook.
The Automated Surface Observing System at Logan International Airport (KBOS) recorded wind speeds to 35 mph and gusts to 51 mph.  In addition, a tree was downed on Broadway in Revere.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Jaffrey Municipal-Silver Ranch Airport (KAFN) recorded wind gusts of 51 mph.  In addition, trees and wires were downed on several roads throughout Cheshire County, including the communities of Richmond, Chesterfield, and Jaffrey.
Trees and wires were downed on Winding Road in Hancock, Poor Farm Road in Francestown, and in Temple.  A piece of sheet metal on the roof of an auto body shop in Brookline was blown off.
The Automated Surface Observing Station at Blue Hill Observatory (KMQE) in Milton, MA recorded wind speeds of 40 mph with gusts to 55 mph.  No damage was reported.
The Automated Surface Observing System at Nantucket Memorial Airport (KACK) recorded wind speeds of 40 mph with gusts to 53 mph.  No damage was reported.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Windham Airport in Willimantic, CT (KIJD) recorded sustained wind speeds of 37 mph and gusts to 56 mph.  In addition, reports were received of large tree limbs blown down onto wires, bringing the wires down as well.

The Automated Surface Observing Station at Beverly Municipal Airport (KBVY) recorded sustained wind speeds to 36 mph and gusts to 46 mph.  In addition, reports were received from Lynn and Salem of large branches blown down onto wires, taking the wires down as well.

The Automated Surface Observing Station at Blue Hill Observatory in Milton, MA (KMQE) recorded sustained wind speeds of 48 mph and gusts to 72 mph.  In addition, a tree was blown down onto a car and a house in Quincy.  Trees and large branches were downed in Braintree and Weymouth.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Taunton Municipal Airport (KTAN) recorded sustained wind speeds of 33 mph and gusts to 52 mph.  In addition, a tree was downed onto two cars in Norton.  A large branch fell through a windshield, another landed on a car in Taunton.  Also in Taunton, multiple trees were downed, including one onto a car and two utility poles were downed.  In Dighton, trees and a large sign were blown down.  A tree was downed in Raynham.

A 53 mph wind gust was recorded on a ham radio operators home weather station in Middleboro.  In addition, many trees were downed in Bridgewater, Brockton, Plympton, East Bridgewater, and Lakeville.  Two utility poles were downed in Bridgewater.

A wind gust of 51 mph was recorded on a ham radio operators home weather station in Dartmouth.  In addition, trees were downed in Dartmouth, Warren, Freetown, Fairhaven, and New Bedford.  Several street lights were downed in New Bedford, including one that landed on a house.  Damage to the house is unknown.
The Automated Surface Observing System at T.F. Green State Airport (KPVD) recorded sustained winds of 44 mph and gusts to 56 mph.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Westerly State Airport (KWST) recorded a wind gust to 49 mph.  In addition, several higher gusts were recorded on amateur radio operators' home weather stations.  Trees and branches were downed in Charlestown, Kingston, and North Kingstown, one branch landed on a car.

In Dartmouth: Rocks and other ocean debris were found on the side of Smith Neck Road.  In addition, oceanwater reached a house with water in neighboring yards on Water Street.  The ocean was up to the level of the sea wall.

Fifteen to twenty inches of snow fell in Washington County.

There were a few brief breaks in visibility between 12:00am EST and 10:00am EST.  Four straight hours of blizzard conditions followed.

Four to fourteen inches of snow fell across western Middlesex County.
Four to eleven inches of snow fell across interior Essex County.

Seven to twenty one inches of snow fell across Cape Cod.  Strong winds also affected the Cape with a sustained wind speed of 44 mph recorded at the AWOS at Provincetown and a 62 mph wind gust recorded on a spotters home weather station.  Several trees and large branches were downed by the combination of high winds and heavy snow.

Loring Road and Commercial, Bridge, and Forrester Streets in Salem were flooded with seawater.  In addition, the commuter rail parking lot in Salem was flooded.  Waves at Deveraux Beach in Marblehead overtopped the seawall, flooding an adjacent parking lot.  Lynn Shore Drive in Lynn was flooded by waves overtopping the seawall.  The intersection of Liberty and Tibet Roads in Danvers was closed because of flooding.  Portions of Route 107 in Saugus were flooded.  Essex and Western Avenues in Gloucester were flooded, as well as Causeway Street and Thatcher Road.

Also in Hull, Moreland and Nantasket Avenues were both flooded.  The intersection of Fore River Avenue and Holbrook Road in Weymouth was flooded with one foot of water. A weather station at an amateur radio operator's home in Barnstable recorded a wind gust of 67 mph.  Also in Barnstable, a tree was downed on Long Pond Road.  The Automated Weather Observing System at Cape Cod Coast Guard Air Station (KFMH) recorded a wind gust of 58 mph.

A weather station at an amateur radio operator's home in Wrentham recorded a wind gust of 62 mph.  Trees were downed in Wrenthm and Brookline.
