Also, Pine Stret was closed from Johns Avenue to Weymouth Street because of downed wires.  Wires were downed across Canterbury Lane in Needham.  A large tree was downed in Stoughton.  In Brookline, a large tree was downed onto wires onto Heath Street, closing the street to traffic.

Amateur radio operators in Malden and North Cambridge recorded wind gusts to 64 mph and 54 mph, respectively, on their home weather stations.  A tree was downed onto a house in Malden.  In Watertown, a tree was downed behind Watertown Mall.  Several trees were downed around Newton, including on Dalby Street, Wendell Road, Manemet Road, Grove Street, and Plymouth Road.  In Melrose, a large tree was downed onto wires on Hickory Street.

A Weatherflow reporting site at Pleasure Bay recorded a wind gust of 69 mph.  The Weatherflow reporting site at Deer Island recorded a wind gust of 60 mph.  The Automated Surface Observing System at Logan International Airport (KBOS) recorded a wind gust of 60 mph.  In Boston, a tree was downed onto East Street and power lines were downed on Red Pine Road.  A large tree was downed onto cars and laying across Blue Hill Avenue.  A tree was downed at the intersection of VFW Parkway and Centre Street in Jamaica Plain.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Blue Hill Observatory and Science Center in Milton (KMQE) recorded wind gusts up to 81 mph.  The media also reported gusts up to 62 mph in Braintree.  No damage was reported.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Taunton Municipal Airport (KTAN) reported wind gusts up to 51 mph.  An amateur radio operator also recorded sustained winds up to 49 mph on their home weather station in Taunton.  Numerous trees were downed in Raynham.  Also, a 50 foot portion of the cafeteria roof at the Merrill School on Pleasant Street was blown off.  Numerous trees were downed throughout Attleboro.  One of these trees was downed onto a car on Reservoir Street.

An amateur radio operator in Brockton recorded a wind gust to 65 mph on their home weather station.  Wires were downed on West Chestnut Street.  In Hanson, a tree was downed onto wires on High Street.  A tree was downed onto wires on Atwood Street in Carver.

Amateur radio operators in Hingham, Scituate, and Plymouth recorded wind gusts of 65, 60, and 62 mph on their home weather stations, respectively.  The Automated Surface Observing System at Plymouth Municipal Airport (KPYM) recorded wind gusts to 52 mph.  The Weatherflow reporting site at Hull recorded a wind gust to 60 mph.  A Weatherflow reporting site in Duxbury recorded a wind gust to 64 mph.  A tree was downed onto wires on Congress Street.  A tree was downed at the intersection of Derby Street and Route 3 in Hingham.  In Scituate, a large tree was downed.

The Automated Surface Observing System at New Bedford Regional Airport (KEWB) recorded wind gusts to 53 mph.  An amateur radio operator in Fall River recorded a wind gust to 51 mph on their home weather station.  In Fall River, large branches were downed onto wires and a tree was downed onto a house on Highland Avenue.  Also, a 40 foot section of roof was blown off the Westall School on Maple Street.  With significant rain occurring at the time, this also resulted in water damage within the school.  A tree was downed on High Hill Road near the intersection with Pine Island Road in Dartmouth.

No wind speed observations were reported from southern Plymouth County, however reports from surrounding areas and damage reports indicate that winds likely reached high wind criteria.  A car port was blown over in Rochester.

Amateur radio operators in Harwich, Eastham, Barnstable, East Falmouth, Chatham, and Marstons Mills reported wind gusts to 64, 62, 62, 56, 55, and 53 mph, respectively, on their home weather stations.  The Automated Weather Observing System at Cape Cod Coast Guard Air Station in Falmouth (KFMH) recorded wind gusts to 58 mph.  Sustained winds up to 41 mph were reported by the general public in East Falmouth and Eastham.  A Weatherflow reporting site in Eastham recorded a wind gust to 62 mph.  No damage was reported.

Law enforcement reported wind gusts up to 64 mph in Scituate.  The media reported gusts to 51 mph in Woonsocket.  A primary power line was downed on East School Street in Woonsocket.  In Glocester, a tree was downed across Snake Hill Road.
An amateur radio operator recorded a wind gust to 52 mph on their home weather station in Coventry.  A tree was downed blocking a road in West Greenwich.
The Automated Surface Observing System at T.F. Green State Airport in Warwick (KPVD) recorded a wind gust to 60 mph.  No damage was reported.
The Weatherflow reporting site at Bristol recorded a wind gust of 63 mph.  No damage was reported.
Amateur radio operators in Richmond and Keene recorded wind gusts of 48 and 33 mph respectively, on their home weather stations.  A tree and wires were downed on East Lake Road in Fitzwilliam.
A tree was downed onto wires on Old Amherst Road in Belchertown.

Amateur radio operators in Westerly and South Kingstown reported wind gusts to 56 and 55 mph, respectively, on their home weather stations.  In Richmond, a tree was downed near Richmond Elementary School on Kingston Road.
An emergency manager reported sustained winds of 40 mph in Manchester.  No damage was reported.

In Salisbury, coastal flooding resulted in structural damage to the ocean side of a building on North End Boulevard.  This road was flooded from #170 to #250 resulting in the mandatory evacuation of about 50 houses.  A barrier beach was breached and significant beach erosion occurred, damaging dunes and sand fencing.  The south end of Atlantic Avenue was impassable with water flowing around and under buildings.  In Gloucester, Atlantic Road was flooded and impassable.  The Good Harbor Beach walkway bridge was damaged.  Significant beach erosion occurred, damaging dunes.  The Lane's Cove breakwater was damaged near Dudley Street.  In Marblehead, the Marblehead Causeway (Ocean Avenue) and Marblehead Neck were flooded and impassable.  In Manchester-by-the-Sea, a pier at Magnolia Beach was damaged.  In Newbury, water flowed around and under buildings through the Beach Center parking lot and down a nearby street for about 200 yards.  Five to ten houses on Annapolis Way, Dartmouth Way, and Southern Boulevard sustained damage to the foundations and stairs.  Significant beach erosion occurred, damaging dunes and sand fencing.  A building on Harvard Way sustained damage to the foundation and stairs.  In Newburyport, significant beach erosion occurred.  In Rockport, numerous streets were flooded and impassable.  Water flowed around and under buildings at Front Beach and near Old Harbor.  Significant beach erosion occurred, damaging dunes, sand fencing, stairs and railings.  A boat ramp at Granite Pier was damaged.  In Salem, debris, rocks, and sand were strewn across the parking lot and walkways at Winter Island Park.

In Revere, Pines Road was inundated by ocean water.  Winthrop Parkway experienced splashover with ocean debris in the road.  In Winthrop, Shirley Street, Tafts Avenue, and Winthrop Shore Drive were flooded with up to two feet of water.  Yirrell Beach at Mugford Street was flooded with water flowing around and under buildings.

In Cohasset, Atlantic Avenue, Oceanside Drive, and the causeway (Summit Avenue) at Jerusalem Road were flooded.  Water one to two feet deep reached up to a couple of houses on Beach Street.  In Hull, numerous streets were flooded and impassable.  Gunrock Street and a street behind Stoney Beach were washed out.  Water flowed around and under several buildings.  At least one building sustained damage to the foundation and stairs.  Streets and houses were flooded on Channel Street, Ocean Avenue, and Nantasket Avenue.  Significant beach erosion occurred, damaging dunes.

In Plymouth, Warren Avenue was flooded near the entrance to the beach.  A road near the north end of White Horse Beach was washed over with two feet of sand.  A house on Taylor Avenue was completely destroyed with wreckage strewn for half a mile.  Foundations and stairs of six to eight buildings were damaged.  Significant beach erosion occurred with damage to dunes, sand fencing, and stairs.  The Pilgrim Sands Motel was flooded with two feet of water in their basement.  The Breakwater parking lot was undermined and eroded.  In Scituate, numerous streets were flooded and impassable, with up to four feet of water.  Moderate to major coastal flooding occurred with depths of water reaching up to 16.6 feet at one point.  Water had flowed up to an apartment building on Cole Parkway.  The Scituate light house was damaged.  Water was flowing around and under houses near Edward Foster Road, Town Way Extension, and Oceanside Road.  Significant beach erosion occurred, damaging dunes, sand fencing, and stairs.  A house on Scituate Avenue was flooded.  The foundation of two buildings were damaged, one at the intersection of Oceanside Road and Tuner Road and the other on Surfside Avenue.  A large hole in Glades Road exposed buried utility lines.  Ocean debris was found on Surfside Road. In Marshfield, numerous streets were flooded and impassable.  Cars were stuck in flood waters on Plymouth Avenue.  Water flowed around and under buildings throughout Marshfield.  Significant beach erosion occurred, damaging stairs.  Brook Street was washed out.  In Duxbury, significant beach erosion occurred, damaging stairs and dunes.  Damage was sustained to the stairs of a building on Ocean Road North.  Water flowed around and under buildings in the High Pines area.  Water flowed through one house on Gurnet Road.  In addition, stairs were damaged on about 15 buildings on Gurnet Road.

In Sandwich, private and public access stairs leading to the beach were washed away.  Water flowed around and under buildings, damaging at least four houses.  One of the houses foundation was undermined and adjacent houses flooded.  Several roads were flooded and impassable.  The firehouse on Route 6A was flooded.  Beach erosion occurred, damaging sand fencing, stairways, and walkways.  In Dennis, Harbor Road was flooded up to two feet deep near Sesuit Harbor.  Route 6A was flooded and impassable at the Dennis/Brewster line.  A parking lot at Corporation Beach was undermined and had collapsed.  Beach erosion occurred, damaging sand fencing.  Dr Botero Road was flooded and had washed out in places.  In Borne, significant beach erosion occurred, damaging stairs of four buildings.  The town access ramp at Phillips Road was washed away.  In Brewster, approximately 20 feet of the parking lot at Ellis landing was lost as the beach washed over the parking lot.  A house adjacent to the parking lot sustained damage to the structure and foundation.  Fifteen feet of parking lot at Breakwater Beach was lost.  Significant beach erosion occurred, damaging dunes, sand fencing, and stairs.  Approximately 10 feet of parking lot at Mants Landing was lost.  In Chatham, significant beach erosion occurred, damaging sand fencing and stairs.  Water flowed under and around buildings at the Fish Pier.  Debris accumulated at the northern end of the pier.  A seasonal cottage on North Beach Island lost its foundation support and stairs and was leaning on its side.  It has been condemned and scheduled for demolition.

Easy and Washington Streets were flooded up to three feet deep.  Water up to two feet deep came up to a couple of houses on Beach Street.  Wauwinet Road near Eat Fire Springs Road flooded.  Water was as far up as the Nantucket Hotel on Easton Street in the Brant Point area.  Main Street was flooded up to the Club Car Restaurant.  Significant beach erosion occurred, damaging sand fencing.

Blizzard conditions were observed on the Automated Surface Observing System at Hanscom Field in Bedford, MA (KBED) for a total of four and a half hours.  End time of this event was estimated due to the loss of wind sensors at almost all ASOS stations in eastern MA.  Prior to the loss of wind data, the highest wind gust observed was 75mph.  No damage was reported.
Blizzard conditions were inferred to have occurred across western Essex County on the basis that blizzard conditions were observed in all surrounding zones.  All times are estimated.

Near blizzard conditions were observed on the Automated Surface Observing System at Beverly Municipal Airport (KBVY) for two to three hours prior to the most intense part of the storm.  Wind sensors were lost during the height of the storm, making verification difficult.  Times are estimated based on surrounding stations and radar data.  Wires were downed in Manchester-by-the-Sea.  The highest wind gust observed was 71 mph at the Weatherflow recording site at Dog Bar Breakwater.
Blizzard conditions were observed on the Automated Surface Observing System at Norwood Memorial Airport (KOWD) for a total of seven and a half hours.
Blizzard conditions were inferred to have occurred across southeastern Middlesex County on the basis that blizzard conditions were observed in all surrounding zones. All times are estimated.

Blizzard conditions were observed on the Automated Surface Observing System at Logan International Airport in Boston, MA (KBOS) for four hours. End time of this event was estimated due to the loss of wind sensors at almost all ASOS stations in eastern MA.  The highest wind gust observed before the loss of the wind sensor was 66 mph at Logan Airport.

Blizzard conditions were inferred to have occurred across eastern Norfolk County on the basis that blizzard conditions were observed in all surrounding zones and based on wind speeds observed by the Automated Surface Observing System at Blue Hill Observatory in Milton, MA (KMQE). All times are estimated.  The highest wind gust was 66 mph at Blue Hill Observatory.

Blizzard conditions were observed on the Automated Surface Observing System at Taunton Municipal Airport (KTAN) for three and a half hours. End time of this event was estimated due to the loss of wind sensors at almost all ASOS stations in eastern MA.

Blizzard conditions were inferred to have occurred across western Plymouth County on the basis that blizzard conditions were observed in all surrounding zones. All times are estimated.  The highest wind gust was 68 mph and was reported by an amateur radio operator on their home weather station in Scituate.  A tree was downed onto a snowmobile in Hanover.  The snowmobile driver was not injured.  Several trees and wires were downed in Halifax.

Blizzard conditions were observed on the Automated Weather Observation System at Cape Cod Coast Guard Air Station in Falmouth, MA (KFMH) for four and a half hours.  The strongest wind gust observed was 69 mph at a Weatherflow measuring site at Sagamore Beach.  Amateur radio observers and a trained spotter recorded wind gusts between 72 and 83 mph on their home weather stations in Falmouth, Hyannis, Marstons Mills, and Mashpee.  The Automated Surface Observing System at Chatham Municipal Airport (KCQX) recorded a wind gust of 61 mph.
Blizzard conditions were observed on the Automated Weather Observation System at North Central State Airport in Smithfield, MA (KSFZ) for a total of five and a half hours.

Near blizzard conditions were observed on the Automated Surface Observing System at TF Green State Airport (KPVD) for two to three hours prior to the most intense part of the storm. Wind sensors were lost during the height of the storm, making verification difficult. Times are estimated based on surrounding stations and radar data.  The highest wind gust observed was 54 mph at a Weatherflow reporting site at Providence Harbor.
Blizzard conditions were observed on the Automated Surface Observing System at Worcester Regional Airport (KORH) for a total of eight hours.  The highest wind gust reported was 65 mph, in Milford.

Near blizzard conditions were observed on the Automated Surface Observing System at Plymouth Municipal Airport (KPYM) for two to three hours prior to the most intense part of the storm. Wind sensors were lost during the height of the storm, making verification difficult. Times are estimated based on surrounding stations and radar data.  The highest wind gust observed was 68 mph recorded by an amateur radio operator on their home weather station.

Blizzard conditions were observed on the Automated Surface Observing System at New Bedford Regional Airport (KEWB) for a total of four and a half hours. End time of this event was estimated due to the loss of wind sensors at almost all ASOS stations in eastern MA.  The highest wind gust recorded was 63 mph reported by an amateur radio operator on their home weather station in Fall River.  Numerous trees and wires were downed in Dartmouth.  Power lines were downed onto a house on Westland Street in New Bedford.  A power pole was downed onto a generator and a camper on Victoria Street in Dartmouth.  A large tree limb and wires were downed onto a car on Rockland Street in New Bedford.  A traffic light was downed into an intersection on Belleville Avenue and a building sign was blown down in New Bedford.

Blizzard conditions were inferred to have occurred across southern Plymouth County on the basis that blizzard conditions were observed in all surrounding zones. All times are estimated.  A tree was downed into a utility pole on Mattapoisett Neck Road in Mattapoisett.
Blizzard conditions were inferred to have occurred across Bristol County on the basis that blizzard conditions were observed in all surrounding zones. All times are estimated.

Blizzard conditions were observed on the Automated Surface Observing System at Newport State Airport (KUUU) for a total of three and a half hours.  The highest wind gust observed was 68 mph recorded by an amateur radio operator on their home weather station in Jamestown.

Blizzard conditions were observed on the Automated Surface Observing System at Hartford-Brainard Airport (KHFD) for a total of three hours.  The highest wind gust observed at Bradley International Airport (KBDL) was 60 mph.
Blizzard conditions were observed on the Automated Surface Observation System at Barnes Municipal Airport in Westfield, MA (KBAF) for a total of three hours.

Blizzard conditions were observed on the Automated Surface Observing System at Manchester-Boston Regional Airport (KMHT) for a total of three hours.  End time of this event was estimated due to the loss of wind sensors at almost all ASOS stations in Southern New England.
Trees and wires were downed onto Route 6A just east of that roads intersection with Route 132.
The Weatherflow reporting site at Quonset Point reported wind gusts up to 63 mph.  No damage was reported.
The Buzzards Bay Buoy recorded wind gusts up to 83 mph.  No damage was reported.

In Marblehead, a parking lot at Devereux Beach was under a foot of fast moving water and overwash.  Atlantic Avenue was closed near the Swampscott line due to coastal flooding and large debris in the road.  Marblehead Neck Causeway (Ocean Avenue) was flooded, closing the road.  Rocks and other ocean debris blocked the roadway.  In Salisbury, significant beach erosion occurred near North End Boulevard, the south end of Atlantic Avenue, and Beach Center.  Water flowed around houses in these areas.  The dune structure on Salisbury Beach experienced major damage.  Beach Road was closed due to flooding.  The 200 block of North End Boulevard was closed due to coastal flooding.  The 700 block of North End Boulevard to Route 1A was closed due to a breach in the seawall.  Several feet of sand were in the road.  The Surf Side Beach Bar and Grill at 25 Broadway was condemned because of structural damage resulting from battering of waves for multiple tide cycles.  Eleventh Street was flooded.  In Essex, Route 133 was closed because the causeway was flooded.  In Lynn, Nahant Parkway and Lynn Shore Drive were closed due to flooding.  In Rockport, a paved parking area at Old Harbor was undermined.  Splashover over the seawalls at Front and Back Beaches was flowing around buildings and depositing debris in the road.  Penzance Road was completely torn up with sheets of pavement washed away.  A driveway in the Back Beach area was undermined.  Beach Street was littered with overwash debris.  The parking lot at Rockport Harbor was undermined with overwash flowing over the tip of Bearskin Neck.   Thurston Place, Marmion Way, and Penzance Road were all flooded with overwash debris in the road.  The seawall was collapsed in some locations.  On Plum Island, two houses were severely undermined and damaged and collapsed into the water.  Additional houses were condemned because of damage sustained.  Along Annapolis Way in Newbury, water flowed in and around houses resulting in damaged foundations, stairs, and decks.  Dartmouth Street was inaccessible because of flooding.  Water flowed around buildings on Harvard Way.  Houses at the ends of Harvard Way and Fordham Way experienced deck and floor collapses, resulting in belongings being deposited onto the beach, water flowed around houses on these streets.  The foundation of one of the houses was undercut after a bulkhead collapsed.  In Swampscott, Lynn Shore Drive was closed due to flooding.  In Salem, Bridge and Commercial Streets were flooded with six inches of coastal water.

In Boston, Morrissey Boulevard was closed in both directions from the University of Massachusetts Boston campus to Freeport Street.  Exit 14 from Interstate 93 northbound was closed due to the flooding on Morrissey Boulevard.  In Winthrop, six roads were flooded up to the curbs with splashover reaching the front steps of houses.  Winthrop Shore Drive was flooded with water and overwash material.  In Revere, Winthrop Parkway was flooded with water and debris.

In Cohasset, several houses on Beach Street were flooded above the basement level.  The parking lot at Sandy Beach was flooded.  Atlantic Avenue, Jerusalem Road, Stockbridge, Bow, and Margin Streets were flooded and impassable.  Rocks and debris were found on the causeway.  Atlantic Avenue was closed at the Hull town line because of debris and water in the road.

In Plymouth, Route 3A was closed between Cliff Street and Clifford Road due to flooding.  A septic system was exposed on the seaward side of Taylor Avenue because of erosion.  Warren Avenue near the Bert's Landing Restaurant was flooded.  Taylor Avenue near Bartlett Pond was flooded.  A sidewalk was undermined at Nelson Street Beach.  Homer Avenue was flooded with so much sand it was almost impassable by car.  In the Long Beach area, rocks and other ocean debris covered almost a quarter of a mile of Route 3A.  Parking lots in this area were at least 50% flooded with lots of rocks and ocean debris and jersey barriers from the edges of the lot were pushed in towards the center of the lot.  In Scituate, the parking lot at Scituate Light was flooded.  Rocks and other debris were reported near a fire hydrant in the parking lot.  Houses were damaged in this area as well.  The Town Way extension was impassable.  Part of Edward Foster Road was closed.  The upper parking area at the Cole Parkway Marina was flooded with between 1 and 2 feet of water.  Central Avenue was flooded and impassable with debris and rocks on the road.  Buildings were damaged along Central Avenue, especially near that roads intersection with Cliff Road.    Turner Road was flooded with two feet of water near Oceanside Drive.  Edward Foster Road between 1st and 2nd cliff flooded.  Oceanside Drive was flooded and impassable.  Cars were stuck in coastal flood waters on Atlantic Avenue.  Cole Parkway and Atlantic Drive were flooded and impassable.  Barratt Street was washed out.  Peggoty Beach experienced significant erosion.  Patios, decks, and other sorts of exterior structure were damaged in the area of Surfside Road.  In Marshfield, the Brant Rock and Esplanade sections were flooded and impassable with rocks and other debris on roadways.  Ocean Street from Colonial Road to Dyke Road had rocks and other debris in the road from significant splashover.  Damage to the seawall at Foster Avenue and Brook Street resulted in those streets flooding.  Numerous coastal streets were flooded with water flowing around the buildings and rocks and other ocean debris on the roads.  In Hull, Atlantic Avenue at Gunrock Avenue was closed for six hours because of at least six inches of water flowing over the road.  Ocean Avenue at Spring Street was flooded and impassable.  Significant erosion of dunes occurred at Nantasket Beach.  Houses and roads along Gunrock Beach were damaged.  A playground on Ocean Avenue was flooded.  Nantasket Beach between W and Y Streets was flooded, with ocean water and sand flowing through houses.  Nantasket Avenue at several locations  was flooded with water and ocean debris.  Warren Street at Nantasket Beach experienced flooding and erosion, exposing concrete foundations.  A sidewalk was undermined and destroyed on Franklin Street near Nantasket Beach.  A side street and a driveway along that side street were washed out near Gunrock Avenue.  This resulted in damage to nearby buildings.  Yards were flooded on both sides of Hampton Circle.  Hull Shore Drive was closed due to flooding.  George Washington Avenue was flooded with water and ocean debris.  A house in the Rockland Street marsh was flooded with water around the house and in the basement.  In Duxbury, Gurnet Road was washed out stranding people in the Gurnet section of Plymouth.

Sandwich experienced the majority of the coastal flooding on Cape Cod.  The Sandwich Boardwalk was flooded.  At Sandwich Marina, water was up to the harbormaster shack.  Foster Road, Spring Hill Road, and River Street flooded.  Houses on Salt Marsh Road were damaged, including a deck destroyed and a foundation undermined.  In addition, several houses were flooded.  An elevated walkway connecting the town beach parking area and the barrier beaches was destroyed.  Minor coastal flooding occurred in Eastham, Wellfleet, Brewster, and Chatham.
Beach Road in Oak Bluffs was undermined near Farm Pond Road at the end of the seawall.  East Chop Drive was flooded with water, rocks, and other ocean debris.
Hulbert Avenue, Washington, Broad, Easton, and Easy Streets were flooded and impassable.  Sheep Pond Road was flooded and water eroded the foundation of a building.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Nantucket Memorial Airport (KACK) recorded sustained winds of 51 mph and gusts to 63 mph.  An amateur radio operator also reported gusts to 63 mph.  No damage was reported.

An amateur radio operator recorded a 58 mph wind gust on their home weather station in Barnstable.  A spotter in East Falmouth recorded a 61 mph wind gust on their home weather station.  The Automated Weather Observation System at Provincetown Municipal Airport (KPVC) recorded sustained wind speeds of 44 mph.  No damage was reported.

The Weatherflow reporting site at Duxbury recorded a wind gust of 58 mph.  A tree was downed onto wires on Indian Trail in Scituate.  In Marshfield, a tree was downed onto wires on Baker Street.  Several trees were downed, one of which blocked half of Forest Street in Norwell.  Numerous trees and wires were downed in Hingham, including a tree on Prospect Street.

A ten to twelve inch diameter tree was downed on Elaine Way in Acushnet.  Wires were downed on Acushnet Avenue in New Bedford.  Amateur radio operators in New Bedford and Fall River recorded wind gusts to 47 mph on their home weather stations.
A tree and two utility poles were downed at the intersection of Russell Street and Brook Road.
A tree was downed onto wires on Summer Street near the Hanover/Rockland town line.  Trees were downed on Chestnut Street in Middleborough.
A tree was downed across Route 140, blocking a portion of the road.
Three to almost nineteen inches of snow fell across Hartford County.
Fifteen to twenty-three inches of snow fell across Tolland County.
Five to eighteen inches of snow fell across Windham County.
Eleven to nearly twenty-three inches of snow fell across northern Bristol County.
Eight to eighteen inches of snow fell across southern Bristol County.
Nine to sixteen inches of snow fell across interior Essex County.
Eight to eighteen inches of snow fell across coastal Essex County.
Three to seven inches of snow fell across western Franklin County.
One to six inches of snow fell across eastern Franklin County.
Four to seven inches of snow fell across western Hampden County.
Two to twenty-one inches of snow fell across eastern Hampden County.
Seven to eight inches of snow fell across western Hampshire County.
One to thirteen inches of snow fell across eastern Hampshire County.
Nine to twenty-two inches of snow fell across western Middlesex County.
Ten to seventeen inches of snow fell across southeastern Middlesex County.
Fourteen to sixteen inches of snow fell across northwestern Middlesex County.
Fourteen to nearly twenty-five inches of snow fell across western Norfolk County.
Twelve to nearly thirty inches of snow fell across eastern Norfolk County.
Ten to twenty-two inches of snow fell across western Plymouth County.
Six to sixteen inches of snow fell across eastern Plymouth County.
Five to twelve inches of snow fell across southern Plymouth County.
Thirteen to eighteen inches of snow fell across Suffolk County.
Eight to twenty-four inches of snow fell across northern Worcester County.
Ten to twenty-four inches of snow fell across southern Worcester County.
One to eleven inches of snow fell across Cheshire County.
Five to sixteen inches of snow fell across eastern Hillsborough County.
Five to twelve inches of snow fell across western and central Hillsborough County.
Six to seven inches of snow fell across Bristol County.
Two to seven inches of snow fell across Newport County.
Five to twelve inches of snow fell across northwestern Providence County.
Five to six inches of snow fell across southeastern Providence County.

A tornado touched down at a car dealership on Route 138 in Stoughton where it was captured by a security camera and recorded on several employees cell phone cameras.  Three RV trailers, weighing about 5000 pounds each, were pushed back about 6 feet against a chain link fence.  One trailer was lifted about 15 feet into a light pole but landed on its wheels with minimal damage.  An aluminum door about 20 feet high and 15 feet wide was blown out of the service garage.  Eyewitnesses reported ceiling tiles being lifted inside the dealership as the tornado passed overhead.  The tornado entered a wooded area just to the northeast of the dealership.  Roughly one quarter of a mile away on Erica Drive and Dean Road, two large pine trees were downed before the tornado dissipated.
Belleville Avenue between Tarkiln Hill Road and Nash Road was flooded and nearly impassable.  The basement of the Urban Grille on Purchase Street was flooded with 10 inches of water.
A foot of water flooded Route 28 in Wareham near the Cranberry Plaza Shopping Center.
Spring Street near the Taber Library was flooded and almost impassable.
Lightning struck a tree outside a house on Colrain Shelburne Road, traveled through the ground and started a fire in the attic of the house.
A tree and wires on Minott Road in Gardner were downed by thunderstorm winds.
The Cooperative Observer in Ashfield, MA reported a large amount of hail fell.  Most of it was three-eighths of an inch in diameter, but a few were as large as three-quarters of an inch.
Lightning struck a house on Jeanine Circle, causing damage to the electric service.
Quarter sized hail was reported near Buckland Mall and lasted for just over 10 minutes.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree onto wires near the Surry town line.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree and wires on Route 119.
Wires were downed on Route 12 at Gap Mountain Road.
A wind gust to 59 mph was reported in West Cummington.

Three students at the MacDuffie School in Granby were struck by lightning while sitting outside at a picnic table. Two students were knocked unconscious and were hospitalized. The third student was further away when the lightning struck and was not directly hit, suffering less serious effects. The students were 16, 17, and 20 years of age. All of the students reovered from their injuries.
Lightning struck a tree in Erving which fell and blocked a portion of Route 2.
A lightning strike ignited a house fire on Haven Hill Road.
A house was struck by lightning on Church Street.
Thunderstorm winds downed trees on wires in Plainfield and Cummington. In Chesterfield, a downed tree blocked Old Chesterfield Road.
Trees were downed in Shelburne Falls on Route 2 at State Road, and in Northampton on the Spring Street extension.
A tree was downed onto wires on Crowl and Neilson Streets.
Trees were downed in Suffield on Hill Street and a few other locations.

State police reported winds gusting up to 40 mph downed three trees and some wires, blocking Foundry Village Road.  Heavy rain over the previous several days had saturated the ground allowing for lighter winds downing trees.
A large tree limb was downed by thunderstorm winds onto Rogers Avenue.
Memorial Drive in Chicopee was flooded.  In addition, Prospect Street was flooded with water four feet deep.
Wires on McKintry Avenue were downed by thunderstorm winds.
In West Springfield, Morgan Road was flooded out.
Trees and wires on Honey Road in Marlow were downed by thunderstorm winds.
A tree and wires on Route 119 in Winchester were downed by thunderstorm winds.

The remnants of Tropical Storm Andrea moved across southeastern Massachusetts, resulting in three to six inches of rain falling across Bristol County.  This produced significant street flooding, particularly in Fall River and New Bedford.||In Fall River, the area of town known as Globe Four Corners was flooded.  Cars were stranded in two feet of water at the intersection of Pleasant and Quarry Streets.  A portion of Route 79 was flooded.  The ramp onto Interstate 195 from Central Street was flooded with two feet of water.  The ramp from Route 24 southbound onto Interstate 195 was flooded with two to three feet of water, one car was stuck in floodwaters.  Davol Street was closed due to flooding.  Plymouth Avenue near Davol Street, Jefferson Street, and Warren Street were all flooded.||In New Bedford, Liberty Street was flooded and impassable from Durfee Street to Parker Street.  Several basements were flooded on Cove Road in New Bedford.  There was one foot of standing water at the intersection of West Rodney French Boulevard and Cove Road.  Cove Road was closed due to tidal and freshwater flooding.
Two to five inches of rain fell across Plymouth County.  Spring Street was flooded with two to three feet of water from the fire station to the Sippican School.
Three to five inches of rain fell across Bristol County.  Up to one and a half feet of water flooded Route 140 south of the Cumberland Farms in Taunton.
A tree was downed at the intersection of Slocum Road and Westwood Drive in Dartmouth, blocking half of the road.
A tree and power lines on Arthur Avenue in Dartmouth were downed by strong winds.
A large tree on Route 1 south was downed by strong winds at the Carter Street off-ramp.

Three to five inches of rain fell across the south Boston metro area.  Grossman Drive and the underpass for the MBTA train tracks were flooded in Braintree.  Also, Forbes Road near the bus terminal was flooded.  In Holbrook, several roads flooded including South Franklin Street, Clara and Loud Roads, and Abington Avenue between Weymouth Street and White Road.
Three to four inches of rain fell across the Boston metro area.  Sargent Street in Boston was flooded.
Two to five inches of rain fell across Middlesex County.  Mount Pleasant Street was flooded under the railroad bridge in Billerica.
Three to five inches of rain fell across Bristol County.  A house on Margin Street in New Bedford was flooded with four feet of water.  River Road near Wood Street was closed due to flooding.

Three to five inches of rain fell across the Providence metro area.  In Providence, the exit ramp for Atwells Avenue from Interstate 95 southbound was flooded with one and a half feet of water.  In North Providence, Cottage Avenue was flooded and impassable.  Also, several basements were flooded along Brook Street.  In Cranston, Park and Reservoir Avenues were flooded and impassable.
Three to five inches of rain fell across Kent County.  The intersection of Groveland Avenue and Route 117 was flooded with six inches of water.
Three to five inches of rain fell across the Providence metro area.  Several cars were stuck in several feet of water on Lisa Ann Circle.
Three to five inches of rain fell across Newport County.  The underpass to the Newport Bridge was flooded and impassable.  A small car was stuck in floodwaters.
Three to six inches of rain fell across Washington County.  In Charlestown, Route 1, Route 112, Old Coach Road, and Klondike Road all were flooded.
Two to five inches of rain fell in Bristol County.  Several streets in Bristol were closed due to flooding.
Three to five inches of rain fell across the Providence metro area.  Several basements were flooded along Lockbridge Street in Pawtucket.
Thunderstorms produced strong winds that downed several trees and snapped tree branches.

A beaver dam on a pond had a catastrophic failure.  This sent a substantial amount of water down a stream and into the Quaboug River, flooding Route 67 and damaging it extensively.  One family was evacuated and the house sustained minor damage.
A house on Hyde Park Avenue was struck by lightning, starting a fire.  The second and third floors were engulfed in flames before the fire department was able to put it out.
A house on South Central Street was struck by lightning, igniting a fire in the attic.  It extended to a bedroom and caused significant structural damage and damaged the chimney.
A tree in Colrain was downed onto wires by thunderstorm winds.
A tree on Ryan Road in Northampton was downed onto a transformer by thunderstorm winds.
A utility pole on Falley Drive was downed by thunderstorm winds.
Several trees and wires were downed by thunderstorm winds throughout Hudson.
Trees and wires on Edgehill and Walcott Streets were downed by thunderstorm winds.
A tree and tree limbs on Hutchins Street were downed by thunderstorm winds.
Trees on Meadow Street and Suffield Road were downed by thunderstorm winds.
Large limbs were downed by thunderstorm winds.
A tree on Forest Street was downed by thunderstorm winds, blocking the street.
A tree was downed by thunderstorm winds blocking all westbound lanes of Interstate 90 at mile marker 124 in Newton.
A tree was downed by thunderstorm winds.
A large tree and wires on Farm Street in Dover were downed by thunderstorm winds.
A tree was downed onto a grill in Walpole.
A large tree was uprooted and downed by thunderstorm winds.
A utility pole was downed by thunderstorm winds.
Trees and wires along Route 6 were downed by thunderstorm winds.
Trees were downed by thunderstorm winds.
A tree on Edgell Road was downed by thunderstorm winds onto a truck.

In Worcester, Maple Avenue was washed out with water flowing into a building.  Emergency managers reported several roads were closed due to flooding.  A garage on Chestnut Avenue was flooded with 8 inches of water.  Central Street was flooded over the curbs and into city hall.  In Leicester, the Grindstone River was out of its banks and flowing over Peter Salem Road.
Route 9 was closed at the the Route 126 underpass due to flooding.
A house on Spring Hill Road has eighteen inches of water in the basement with water still rising.
One to two feet of water flooded Route 1 northbound in Danvers.  In Peabody, a car was stuck in flood waters on Roosevelt Street.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell in Greenfield.
Penny size hail fell along Interstate 291.
Lightning struck a tree, knocking it down onto a house.
Lightning struck a house on East Street in Hingham, igniting a fire.  The amount of damage to the home is unknown at this time.
A tree on Conway Road was downed by thunderstorm winds.
A tree on Russell Road was downed by thunderstorm winds.  A tree and utility pole were downed, blocking Route 112.
A tree on Route 5 was downed by thunderstorm winds, blocking a portion of the road.
Two trees were downed in South Deerfield by thunderstorm winds.
A large tree was downed by thunderstorm winds.
A tree on Maple Street was downed onto power lines by thunderstorm winds.
A tree and wires were downed onto a pool house on Jackson Avenue by thunderstorm winds.  In addition, a tree was downed blocking Winona Street.
Nickel size hail fell in northern Manchester.
Lightning struck a camper, then a shed on Labelle Street, igniting a fire in the shed.
A tree and wires on Mountain Spring Road were downed by thunderstorm winds.
A tree and wires were downed by thunderstorm winds at the intersection of Routes 74 and 320 and on Fisher Hill Road.
Multiple cars became stuck in flood waters on Route 116 and several basements were flooded on North Pleasant Street.
A house at 57 Harkness Road was struck by lightning, which ignited a fire.  The house sustained minor damage before it was extinguished.

River Road in Westmoreland was flooded.  Route 12A was washed out and flooded between in multiple locations in Alstead and Surry, including between Gilsum Road and Webster Road in Surry.  Gilsum Mine Road was flooded and impassable in multiple locations in Alstead.  Route 123 was closed at Sargent Road in Marlow due to flooding and debris in the road.  Portions of North, Thayer Brook, and Walpole Valley Roads in Alstead were closed due to flooding.  Two brooks overflowed their banks along Sand Pond Road in Marlow.  The road and one house were flooded.
Eight lifeguard stands were blown over on Horseneck Beach in Westport.  Also, a large branch was downed onto Balsam Street in Fairhaven.
Wires on Quaker Meeting House Road were downed by thunderstorm winds.
Two trees on Moses Road were downed by thunderstorm winds.
A tree and wires along Grant Hill Road in Tolland were downed by thunderstorm winds.  Three inch diameter branches also were downed by thunderstorm winds in nearby Ellington.

Quarter to half dollar size hail fell on Main Street, accumulating up to two inches in spots.  A car on Fairview Avenue was damaged with numerous hail dents.  There were also several reports of nickel size hail in the area of Riverdale Road.  About 500 cars at the Balise family of car dealerships were damaged.  Damage ranged from minimal to extensive.  Further damage was found two weeks later, when heavy rain fell through small holes in the roof of Chestnut Middle School, resulting in water damage.
Penny to quarter size hail fell, covering parts of the driveway.
A tree was downed onto a car on Elm Street in West Springfield.  In addition, a window was broken on Main Street, presumable from the windblown large hail.
Route 114 in Warren was closed due to flooding.
Numerous roads throughout town were closed due to flooding.

In Westfield, several cars were stuck in flood waters near Westfield Industrial Park Road.  Several water rescues occurred.  East Mountain Road, North Elm Street, and Meadow Street were flooded with cars stuck in the flood waters.  Canal Drive was closed after flooding caused a section of the road to collapse.  In Holyoke, a section of Northampton Road was washed out.  Lyman, Walnut, Cabot, and Commercial Streets were all flooded.  A car was submerged at the intersection of Cabot and Commercial Streets, occupants had to be rescued.  Route 5 (or Riverdale Street) in West Springfield was flooded.  In Chicopee, Broadway at Saint James Avenue was closed because of flooding.  Meadow Street and Meeting House Road also were flooded.
Route 10 and Route 189 in Granby were flooded with cars stuck on both roads.  In Windsor Locks, the Farmington River overflowed its banks near the junction of Interstate 91 and Route 159.

Lightning struck the medical office building on the campus of Baystate Mary Lane Hospital in Ware, blowing out the building's electrical panel.  In addition, three people who were on the telephone at the time of the strike reported feeling numbness and a tingling in their arms.  All three walked over to the hospital to be checked out and were fine.
School Street was flooded in front of town hall.  Several cars got stuck in the flood waters.

A storm survey team from the National Weather Service in Taunton, MA confirmed that a microburst occurred in the town of Agawam.  There were two areas of straight line wind damage.  One was in the area of Harvey Johnson Blvd where several trees were downed, a few onto houses.  The more significant area of damage was the area around Meadow Street where 40 to 50 trees were uprooted and 6 to 12 vehicles were crushed by the fallen trees.  Wires were downed in both areas.  There were no reports of significant structural damage or injuries or fatalities.

In West Springfield, Route 20 flooded just west of Elm Street and also near Ohio Avenue with nearly two feet of water.  It was closed in some spots.  Manhole covers also popped off in several places.  Portions of Federal and Worthington Streets in Springfield were closed due to flooding.  Sargent, Canal, and Dwight Streets in Holyoke were closed due to flooding.  East Mountain Road was closed on the Westfield/Southwick line due to flooding.  Also in Westfield, Lockhouse Road and Archer Street were flooded with up to 8 inches of water.  In Agawam, Route 187 at North West Street was flooded and impassable.
The intersection of Routes 202 and 33 were flooded with over a foot of water.
A tree on Pine Street was downed by thunderstorm winds.
A tree on North Lowell Street in Methuen was downed by thunderstorm winds.  Also, a large tree limb was downed onto Curtis Street near the intersection with Jackson Street.

A tree and wires were downed onto a fence on Warwick Street in Lynn.  Also, an eight inch diameter tree branch was downed and blew into a house, the house sustained minor damage.  Several other tree limbs were downed on Lynnfield Street and Savory Street.
Two feet of water flooded portions of Route 2 in Fitchburg.
Moore Street in Lowell was closed due to flooding.
Amesbury Road in Haverhill was flooded.  Jackson and Swan Streets in Methuen were closed due to flooding.
Walnut Street in Peabody was closed due to flooding.  In Beverly, the Cummings Center parking lot flooded and was inaccessible from Route 62.
Mount Pleasant Street in Billerica was closed at the railroad bridge due to flooding.
At least one foot of water flooded Route 128 near the Sudbay's Automotive Center.  All lanes were flooded except for the breakdown lane, where cars were still able to get through.

An EF1 tornado touched down on Hayden Station Road in Windsor and continued moving northeastward through portions of Windsor Locks and across the Connecticut River, ending in the 200 block of Main Street in East Windsor.  ||The roof was blown off a warehouse on Hayden Station Road in Windsor.  Numerous trees were downed near Raymond Road and Alicia Terrace, including some that were downed onto cars and houses.  Shingles were blown off houses on Preston Road and Gaylord Road.  As the tornado traveled northeastward, tobacco tents were ripped off the tobacco fields and some tobacco was flattened.  This can be seen from Interstate 91.  Several eyewitnesses reported debris being lofted into the air and noise that sounded like a freight train as the tornado moved through.  While much of the damage was rated EF-0, there were several small areas of EF-1 damage.  EF-1 damage included a sports bubble collapsing at Sports World in East Windsor and blowing onto Interstate 91, blocking two lanes on the southbound side.  Additionally, reports were received of a semi truck that was blown over on Interstate 91 south at exit 44 in East Windsor.

An EF-0 tornado briefly touched down in Enfield.  This tornado was associated with the same storm that produced the EF-1 tornado in Windsor earlier in the day.  There was scattered tree damage that began on Glen Arden Lane, then crossed Hazard Avenue and continued northeast to Heron Road, ending at Taylor Road.

Three to four inches of rain fell across Cheshire County, some locations receiving that much in one hour.  This resulted in widespread flooding.  In Westmoreland, numerous roads were flooded and many were closed including Route 63 from South Village Road to Route 12, Route 12 from Route 63 to the Keene line, Depot Road, Eagle Road, London Cross Road near Route 12, and areas along Route 61.  The Mill brook overflowed its banks at the intersection of Route 12 and Aldrich Road.  Up to one foot of water and debris flooded the road.  Twenty-five to thirty campers were evacuated from the campground on Route 63 due to flooding.  Part of Route 12 was washed out in the South Village area of Westmoreland.  One lane of Route 63 at Chickering Road was washed out.  Part of Cross Road also was washed out.  The River Road north bridge near the Walpole town line was washed away.  Emergency personnel evacuated parts of the South Village area of Westmoreland.  In Walpole, the intersection of Watkins Hill and County Roads was flooded with over a foot of water.  North Road was closed at Matt Brook.  Several basements were flooded in Gilsum on Vessel Rock Road and Route 10.  Part of North Road in Alstead was closed due to flooding.  Other roads that were closed are Route 123 from Marlow Village to the Alstead line in Marlow, Route 12A from Carpenter to Walpole Valley Road in Surry, and Route 123 at Gilsum Mine Road in Alstead.  In Alstead, Thayer Brook Road near Corbin Road, Route 12A north of Walpole Valley Road, Route 123 from Gilsum Mine Road to the Marlow town line, and South Woods Road were all closed.  A state of emergency was declared for Cheshire county because of the flooding.
An aluminum dock on Beaver Lake was overturned by thunderstorm winds.
Lightning struck a house on Round Hill Road and another on Country Club Way, igniting fires.  No information could be found on the extent of damage to the houses.
Lightning struck the building, causing electrical damage.  Residents were evacuated briefly while firefighters investigated.
A tree on Ledyard Road and two trees on Albany Avenue were downed by thunderstorm winds.  A telephone pole on Albany Avenue also was downed by the thunderstorm winds.

Davis Street was flooded with a car stranded in its flood waters.  Ralston Street was flooded with three feet of water.  Parking lots off of Winchester Street were flooded with water up to the car doors.

The NWS survey team found a discontinuous damage path approximately eleven miles long and 100 yards wide that extended from Andover to Mansfield, Connecticut.  Most of the damage was to trees.  Trees were both uprooted and in other parts of the path tops were snapped off the trees.  The only structural damage was to a sheet metal barn that was torn apart.

A severe thunderstorm downed several trees and large branches on Mountain Spring Road in Tolland.  While several eyewitnesses reported seeing a funnel cloud, the survey team found no evidence of a tornado touching down.  All of the downed trees were blown down in the same direction indicating straight line winds.
Three feet of water flooded Love Lane in Hartford.  A car was stuck in flood waters on Lyme and Palm Streets.

A 45 year old mail carrier died as a result of heat illness on July 6th.  Temperatures in the area had climbed above 90 for the 3rd day in a row on the 5th, when the mail carrier was found and transported to the hospital.  The high humidity levels resulted in heat indices above 90 degrees for the daylight hours and heat indices above 96 degrees for 8 to 9 hours beginning at 11am.  The event start time indicates when heat indices climbed to 100 degrees and the event end time is the time at which he was found collapsed.  He was pronounced dead the following morning at Massachusetts General Hospital.
In Attleboro, the intersection of Maple and South Main Streets was flooded.  A street partially collapsed near the new Walmart on Broadway in Raynham.  In New Bedford, Maplewood Avenue flooded.
Atwood Avenue and Pontiac Avenue in Cranston were flooded.  A car was stuck in the flood waters on Pontiac Avenue.
Several eight inch diameter tree limbs on West Street were downed by thunderstorm winds.
Trees and wires on Mashamoquet and Hampton Roads were downed by thunderstorm winds.
Trees and wires on Putnam Pike and Lake Road were downed by thunderstorm winds.
Wires on South Street were downed by thunderstorm winds.
Trees and wires on Mashentuck Road were downed by thunderstorm winds.
Lightning struck a house on Tracey Lane, igniting a fire.
Lightning struck a tree near a house on Morrow Street.  The lightning traveled along the invisible fence line to the house, damaging the invisible fence circuitry.
Lightning struck an apartment building in Mansfield, knocking out a fire alarm system.
Lightning struck a detached garage on Bonnie Avenue, igniting a fire.  There were no vehicles in the garage but there was damage to other household possessions and belongings.
Lightning struck a house on Elmwood Street, igniting a fire.  The house sustained minor damage.
Branches on Plain Street were downed by thunderstorm winds.
Trees on Fuller Shores were downed onto wires by thunderstorm winds.
A tree was downed by thunderstorm winds at the intersection of Derek Drive and Route 3A.
Route 146 was flooded at Twin River Road.
Lightning struck a large, multi-family house on Butler Avenue, igniting a fire.
The Weatherflow observing site at Sabin Point recorded a thunderstorm wind gust to 41 mph.  No damage was reported.
The sailing vessel Eyebrow reported a 42mph wind gust.  No damage was reported.
Cars were flooded out in the parking lot of Deerfield Academy.
Montague City Road in Montague was closed due to flooding.  Briggs Brook overflowed its banks in Erving, flooding Farley Road and the Farley Ridge area on the Erving/Millers Falls Town line.
The westbound lane of Route 9 was closed due to flooding.
Main Street in Cambridge was closed due to flooding.
Columbia Road was closed at the intersection with Hamilton Street due to flooding.  The deepest water was three feet deep.
Route 2 and Interstate 495 were flooded with six inches of water.
Route 38 was closed because of downed power lines.
Quarter sized hail fell on Route 133 near the Andover/Lowell town line.
An eight inch diameter tree limb was downed by thunderstorm winds onto Route 121.
Two trees on Washington Street were downed by thunderstorm winds.
A tree on Route 135 East near Wellesley College was downed by thunderstorm winds.  Another tree on Chatham Circle and power lines on Howe Street also were downed by thunderstorm winds.
A large branch on Forest Street and a tree on Malden Street were downed by thunderstorm winds.
Minor street flooding occurred in the area near Upper Union Street.  The right lane of King Street to the Interstate 495 south exit ramp was also flooded.

A microburst occurred in the northwestern part of Greenfield and the southeastern portions of Leyden and Colrain, downing numerous trees and wires.  Barton, Country Club, Bernardston, Plain, South Green River, Nelson, and Smead Hill Roads were all affected with a few trees that were downed onto houses.  A utility pole was downed on Barton Road.
WCVB-TV Channel 5 in Boston reported that lightning struck a house on Clifton Avenue, setting the garage on fire.
Heavy rain fell across Greenfield and Bernardston, flooding several roads and washing out several dirt roads in Bernardston and Stetson Drive in Greenfield.  All washed out roads were closed.

A complex of showers and thunderstorms developed over the Wellesley/Needham area.  These storms moved very slowly, if at all, producing three to four inches of rain over the region in 1 to 2 hours time.  This resulted in widespread flash flooding across both cities.  Several streets, including a few major highways were closed due to flooding including:  Washington Street, Route 9, Route 16, Route 128 at exit 19, Great Plain Avenue, and Weston Road.  Many cars were stuck in flood waters on these roads and across intersections.  Numerous basements also were flooded in this region.
Route 9 was flooded in both directions at Route 126, making Route 9 impassable.  Speen Street at Cochituate Road was also flooded with a car stuck in the flood waters there.
Heavy rain fell flooding a portion of Spring Street in front of the Shaw's supermarket in West Roxbury.  A car got stuck in these flood waters.
Heavy rain fell across the metro west region, flooding Nahatan Street at the railroad bridge with several feet of water.  A car was stuck in the flood waters.
Two feet of water flooded Route 28 in front of the fire station.  The road was closed for approximately an hour while the water receded.
Lightning struck the bell tower at Bethany Congregational Church in Quincy, damaging one of the pinnacles and sending stone debris to the ground and through the ceiling of the church.

Another round of heavy rain, resulted in renewed flooding across Wellesley and Natick.  Natick flooding reports will be in another entry for Middlesex County.  In Wellesley, many roads were flooded, including: Wellesley Avenue, Brook, Washington, Cottage and Worcester Streets, and Ingraham, Dover, and Amherst Roads.

Another round of heavy rain resulted in renewed flooding across Wellesley and Natick.  Information on flooding in Wellesley can be found in a similar report for Norfolk County.  In Natick, a car became stuck in flood waters on South Main Street.  Flooding occurred under the Willow Bridge.  Route 9 near the Natick Police Department, Pearl Street, and Plain Streets were all flooded and impassable.

Heavy rain fell across Coventry, RI resulting in substantial flash flooding.  Route 117 was flooded at several points, including near Route 116 under the railroad trestle, near South Main, and near Paine Memorial Field.  Many cars became stuck in flood waters along Route 117.  The area near 1070 Tiogue Avenue was flooded and impassable.  The intersection of Hopkins Hill Road and Tiogue Avenue was flooded with four cars stuck in the flood waters.  The intersection of Laurel Avenue and Washington Street was flooded and impassable.  Hopkins Hill Road was closed due to flooding between South Main Street and Route 3.

A Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation employee observed a waterspout on Quabbin Reservoir in New Salem, MA.  He was able to snap two pictures of the storm, one showing a funnel and another showing the funnel extended down to the water.  The time has been approximated based on radar imagery.  The waterspout was very short lived, never hit land, and did no damage and injured no people.  Winds aloft were not conducive for tornadic development, but the environment was unstable and a surface front was moving through the region.
The Providence Journal reported that two horses died in a barn fire in Hopkinton caused by a lightning strike.  The horses were 6 and 17 years old.
Several streets were flooded with four to eight inches of water.  A car was stuck in flood waters on Golden Hill Street.
Meadow Street was flooded and impassable.  A car was stuck in the flood waters.

Lightning struck near a house on Bay Path Road.  While several homeowners claimed to have experienced electrical problems with the lightning strike, firefighters found no damage within the houses.  Two teenagers (one male, one female) outside manning a yard sale felt the lightning shock.  One (male) declined transportation to the hospital, the other (female) was transported and kept overnight for observation.
Plainfield Pike was flooded with water about six inches deep at the ramp to Interstate 295.

Heavy rain over the same part of Rhode Island for the second day in a row resulted in widespread flash flooding across much of Kent County and Cranston.  Information on flooding in Cranston can be found in a separate event entry for Providence County.  In Coventry this included, Route 102 flooded with up to a foot of water, numerous roads flooded with one to two feet of water, including Route 117, Hopkins Hill and Sandy Bottom Roads, and Laurel and Tiogue Avenues, with cars stuck in flood waters on all of those roads.  Hopkins Hill Road, Sandy Bottom Road, and Route 33 were later closed.  Route 116 (Knotty Oak Road) was washed out at Gervais Street.  In West Greenwich, Route 102 was closed at the Interstate 95 interchange with several feet of water flooding the road.  A couple was rescued from a stranded car on Route 3 near the high school.  In Warwick, three feet of water flowed over Bald Hill Road.  Post Road and Airport Road near T.F. Green Airport were flooded and impassable.  Parts of Post Road were closed. Heavy rain over the same part of Rhode Island for the second day in a row resulted in widespread flash flooding across much of Kent County and Cranston.  Information on flooding in Kent County can be found in a separate event entry for Kent County.  In Cranston, a car became stuck in flood waters in a rotary, stranding a man on the roof of the car. Dean Estates apartment buildings were evacuated by boat by the fire department after flood waters inundated the basement/garden level apartments up to the ceilings.  When firefighters arrived at the apartments, water was already four feet deep.  One firefighter was injured when the first floor collapsed because of the basement flooding.  About 60 people were evacuated from the complex.  One lane of Budlong Road was damaged by flooding.  Reservoir and Pontiac Avenues were flooded and impassable. A 65 car pile up occurred on Interstate 290 westbound near exit 14 in Worcester during the early morning hours.  Light freezing rain and freezing drizzle was occurring at the time, resulting in slick roads.  Thirty-five to forty people were injured, only two seriously.  The crash scene was 1500 feet long and included two tractor trailers and two large commercial trucks.  The interstate was closed for four and a half hours.  Nearby, another accident occurred on Route 9 in Northboro just east of the Route 20 interchange.  Twenty-five cars were involved in that crash but no serious injuries were reported.

The Automated Surface Observing Station at Nantucket Memorial Airport (KACK) recorded sustained wind speeds from 26 to 41 mph and frequent gusts up to 53 mph.  This combined with heavy snow reduced visibilities below a quarter mile.

The Automated Weather Observing System in Marshfield (KGHG) recorded frequent wind gusts up to 43 mph.  This combined with heavy snow and resulted in near zero visibilities.  The combination of winds and heavy snow downed wires on Ocean Street in Marshfield.

The Automated Weather Observation Station at Provincetown Airport (KPVC) recorded sustained winds up to 35 mph and frequent wind gusts up to 48 mph.  These winds combined with heavy snow, reducing visibilities below one quarter mile.  Similar conditions were reported at Chatham Municipal Airport (KCQX).
Water was flowing around and under buildings along a portion of Atlantic Avenue in Salisbury.

Wires were downed on Maxson Hill Road in Hopkinton.
Wires were downed in the area of Mineral Spring Avenue at Spicer Street.

Portions of several shore roads were closed due to coastal flooding around the time of high tide. This included Gunrock Avenue and Atlantic Avenue in Hull, Central Avenue in Scituate, and Warren Avenue (Route 3A) in Plymouth.
Foster and Spring Hill Roads were impassable due to coastal flooding.

Moderate coastal flooding affected Plymouth County during the morning high tide. Many shore roads were closed and impassable due to water and debris. In Scituate, this included Seventh Avenue, Marshfield Avenue, River Street, Border Street, Surfside Road, Oceanside Road, and Turner Road. In Hull, this included Atlantic Avenue, and the Hull Shore Drive extension.  Pemberton Point was inaccessible. On Nantasket Avenue, one car was stranded and ocean water flooded at least one basement. In Plymouth, Route 3A in the Long Beach area was closed, as was Taylor Avenue in the area of Hilltop Avenue. A lifeguard shack was damaged by wave action. In Marshfield, coastal flooding closed the Esplanade area, Ocean Street from Samoset Avenue to Reed Street, Bay Avenue, Canal Street, Plymouth Avenue at West Brook Street, and Old Ferry Street. The Bay Avenue sea wall opening lost its batter boards in the Avon Street area, which resulted in flooding. In Duxbury, Gurney Road was flooded and impassable.
Morrissey Boulevard and Neponset Circle in Boston were flooded and temporarily closed.

Moderate coastal flooding impacted eastern Norfolk County. In Cohasset, Atlantic Avenue was closed as was Margin Street and Jerusalem Road at Bow Street. In Quincy, the storm surge backed into the Neponset River, which produced considerable flooding on Hancock Street. One car was stranded.

Moderate coastal flooding impacted eastern Essex County. In Swampscott, Route 129 (Atlantic Avenue) was closed in the area of Preston Beach. The Marblehead Causeway and Devereaux Beach area in Marblehead was closed due to flooding. In Ipswich, Jeffrey Neck Road, Island Park Road, Water Street, Eagle Hill Road, Argilla Road, and Mulholland Drive were flooded. In Lynn, a portion of Lynn Shore Drive was flooded near the rotary. Linden Road, Summer Street, and Route 107 at Western Avenue were flooded. In Salem, Bridge Street and Commercial Street were flooded, as was Route 133 in Gloucester from Western Avenue to Bond Street. In Salisbury, Ocean Front Road, Beach Road, Ferry Road, and Route 1A by Old County Road were closed due to flooding. In Rockport, the end of the breakwater collapsed, which took down a navigation aid.
Portions of several roads along Nantucket Harbor including Easy Street, Broad Street, and Washington Street were flooded and impassable.

In Sandwich, portions of several roads were flooded and impassable including Foster Road, Spring Hill Road, Dewey Avenue, River Street, and part of Route 6A near the Riverview School. Town Neck Beach and the boardwalk were also flooded. In Wellfleet, Summit Avenue and Old Wharf Road were impassable.

The Automated Surface Observing Systems (ASOS) at Chatham Municipal Airport (KCQX), Barnstable Municipal Airport in Hyannis (KHYA), and Cape Cod Coast Guard Air Station in Falmouth (KFMH) recorded visibilities at or below one quarter mile and frequent wind gusts over 35 mph.  These ranged from a peak wind gust of 49 mph at KCQX to 70 mph at KHYA.  Sustained winds were also very strong with the ASOS at KHYA recording 43 mph sustained winds for a period of time.  The strongest winds occurred coincident with the blizzard conditions, though gustier winds lasted a couple of hours longer than the snow did. Snowfall amounts were modest, though given the winds, very difficult to measure.  Roughly 4-6 of snow was reported.  Wires were downed onto a structure on Foster Road in Sandwich resulting in a fire.  Also, wires were downed in West Yarmouth.  A utility pole and wires were downed on Highbank Road in Yarmouth.  Wires were downed in Mashpee on Mashpee Neck Road and on Bank Street in Harwich.  A tree was downed onto a house on Casey Street in Yarmouth.  The top half of a tree was downed onto Bayport Road in West Harwich. A tree and wires were downed onto Depot Street in Dennis.  Trees were downed in Brewster on Main Street and on Long Pond Road near Route 137.  Wires were downed onto Stony Brook Road in Brewster.  A tree was downed onto a house in South Dennis.

The Automated Surface Observing System at Martha's Vineyard Airport (KMVY) recorded visibilities less than a quarter of a mile and winds gusting frequently over 35 mph and as high as 61 mph.  Sustained winds also were strong and the ASOS at MVY recorded a period of 48 mph sustained winds.  The strongest winds continued for another hour or two beyond the end of the blizzard conditions.  Snowfall amounts were modest though difficult to measure.  Two to four inches of snow was reported.  No damage was reported.

The Automated Surface Observing Systems at Nantucket Memorial Airport (KACK) recorded visibilities at or below one quarter mile and frequent wind gusts over 35 mph and as high as 82 mph at the peak of the blizzard conditions. Sustained winds were also very strong with the ASOS at KACK recording sustained wind speeds of 56 mph.  The strongest winds occurred coincident with the blizzard conditions, though gustier winds lasted a couple of hours longer than the snow did.  Snowfall amounts were highest on Nantucket with 8-10 inches reported.  A large branch was downed onto Highland Avenue, blocking the road.  Several large branches were downed on the east end of Nantucket Island.  Wires were downed, resulting in 1200 customers without power.  Milestone Road was blocked by multiple downed trees as well as snow drifts.

A trained spotter reported wind gusts up to 60 mph in Plymouth.  Additionally, the Automated Surface Observing System at Plymouth Municipal Airport recorded sustained wind speeds of 35 mph and wind gusts of 52 mph.  A tree and wires were downed onto State Road 3A in Plymouth.
The Automated Surface Observing System at Blue Hill Observatory and Science Center in Milton (KMQE) recorded sustained winds of 41 mph.  No damage was reported.

The Automated Surface Observing System at T.F. Green State Airport in Warwick (KPVD) recorded sustained wind speeds of 44 mph.  Winds gusted to 58 mph at a National Ocean Service site at Conimicut Point.  No damage was reported.

In Chatham, the Fishing Pier parking lot was flooded.  And in Dennis, Sesuit Harbor parking lot flooded and the Chapin Beach access ramp eroded away.
A tree was downed onto Fayerweather Street in Cambridge.

These winds resulted in downed tree limbs and power lines on Allston and Rutherford Streets, as well as on Bronx Road.  In addition, these winds greatly exacerbated a structure fire in the Back Bay (ended up as a 9 alarm fire), in which 2 firefighters were killed and 13 others were injured.

In Fall River, several cars were stuck at the intersection of Plymouth Avenue and Globe Street.  Davol and Central Streets near the carousel were flooded and blocked off by local authorities.  Interstate 195 east at the base of the Braga Bridge was flooded out.  A car was stuck in flood waters at the intersection of Tucker Street and Rhode Island Avenue.  Langley Street was closed due to flooding.  In Somerset, one lane of Route 103 and the grass in the area was flooded with running water.  In New Bedford, Phillips Road was flooded near the 7-11 store because of clogged storm drains.  River Road was flooded from Howard Avenue to Sylvia Street.  Route 18 south was closed due to flooding near Purchase Street.  Four cars were stuck in flood waters on Acushnet Avenue.  Cars were going the wrong way on Route 18 in order to avoid the flooding. The intersection of Belleville Avenue and Sawyer Street was flooded with one and a half to two feet of water.  The intersections of Dean and Purchase Streets and Sawyer and Purchase Streets were flooded with three feet of water.  Multiple cars were stuck in flood waters throughout town.  The back of New Bedford Police Headquarters was flooded and impassable, police were advised to avoid the area and only park in front of the building.  The intersection of Coggeshall Street and Purchase Street was flooded and impassable.  The Route 18 ramp to Weld Street was closed due to flooding.  The intersection of Liberty and Hunter Streets was flooded with two and a half feet of water.  West Rodney French Boulevard was flooded and impassable.    In Acushnet, Hamlin Street was flooded near the bridge.  A portion of Middle Road was flooded and closed.  In Freetown, the ramp from Chace Road to Route 140 was closed due to flooding.  In Dartmouth, extensive flooding occurred on Hawley Drive and adjacent side streets.  Seminole Road at Masssasoit Lane was flooded and impassable.  Hawthorne Street west of Brownell Avenue and Clarence Street were flooded.  In Westport, Route 6 was closed near Boar's Head due to flooding.

Three to five inches of rain fell across Bristol County.  This resulted in flash flooding across most of the county.  In Bristol, Franklin, Chestnut, and James Streets were flooded.  Route 114 near the Mount Hope Bridge and the Lobster Pot was closed due to flooding.  Ward Street was flooded and closed.  One house was evacuated at the end of the street. Several basements also were flooded.  In Warren, Main Street was flooded with 4 inches of water and Market Street was flooded with 6-8 inches of water.  Homestead Avenue was flooded with three feet of water.  Long Wharf Drive and Columbus Street were flooded with one foot of water.

Four to five inches of rain fell across portions of Washington County.  This resulted in flash flooding in Westerly.  Canal Street was flooded.  Spring Brook overflowed its banks in the White Rock section of Westerly.  Water overflowed four to five yards nearing the foundations of those houses.  The Pawcatuck River also overflowed its banks in the White Rock section of town.  White Rock Road had 2-3 inches of flowing water over the road near a soccer field entrance.
Montello Street was flooded and impassable.
County Street/Route 140 was closed near Pete S Market due to flooding.

Boston Road was closed near Brian Road due to flooding.  A culvert clogged, resulting in backwater flooding and a subsequent collapse of the culvert and the nearby section of road.  News reports indicated at least 1 flooded basement, and flood waters went into the backyards of some homes. This area of road was closed for several of days during repairs.
Wyman Street was closed due to flooding.
Gould Road was closed due to flooding.

Dartmouth Street was washed out between Rockland and Spooner Streets.  The road was closed for repairs as the asphalt washed away.  In Acushnet, Main Street near Clems Way was flooded and impassable.

A significant portion of Peacedale Village in South Kingstown was flooded and culverts were beyond full.  Low buildings were being sandbagged to protect them.  In Exeter, Route 102 north of Route 2 was flooded with over a foot of water.

A large limb was downed onto Worthington Street.  Also an awning was blown off a building on Chestnut Street, damaging a car.

Southgate, Bellevue, Austin, and Southbridge Streets were flooded and impassable.  Grafton Street was flooded with 8 inches of water from Barclay Street to Interstate 290 with numerous manhole covers popped off.  Harding Street and West Boylston Street were flooded with up to 8 inches of water.  Cars were stuck in flood waters on Quinsigamond Avenue and Plantation Street.  Numerous basements were flooded on Water Street.  Several lanes of Interstate 290 were flooded at Lincoln Square.
Route 2 was closed at the Lincoln/Concord line due to flooding.
Six to twelve inches of water flooded the intersection of Pierpont and Main Streets.
Trees were down on Nagler Cross Road and on Route 20 near Route 112.  One of the trees was downed onto a car and another onto wires.
Power lines on South Meadow Road were downed by thunderstorm winds.  Trees and power lines along Route 20 were downed as well.
Portions of Route 20 were flooded and impassable.
A tree was downed onto a trailer home on Springfield Street.  A tree on Meadow Road was downed by thunderstorm winds.
A tree on High Street was downed by thunderstorm winds, blocking the road.  Trees and wires along Prospect Avenue were downed as well.
Several trees on Route 57 were downed by thunderstorm winds.
A large tree and power lines on Elmwood Road were downed by thunderstorm winds.
Large branches along Route 202 were downed by thunderstorm winds.
Trees and wires on Normandy and Greenwich Roads were downed by thunderstorm winds.  These winds also downed a tree onto a house on Prynnwood Road.
Lightning struck a house on Prospect Street, setting it on fire.
A tree was downed onto a car on Shaker Road by thunderstorm winds.
Trees and wires on George Wood Road were downed by thunderstorm winds.
Trees and wires on North Maple Street were downed by thunderstorm winds.
A tree was downed onto wires on Jobs Hill Road.
A microburst occurred with winds 80-90 mph downing numerous trees and wires on Interstate 195, Goose Lane, and Cedar Mill, Reed and Mile Hill Roads.
A tree was downed onto wires on Route 320 near the Willington/Mansfield line.
Trees and wires on Jonathan Lane were downed by thunderstorm winds.
Trees and wires on Westwood Road and Codfish Falls Road were downed by thunderstorm winds.
The entry to the Meditech building on Cochituate Road was flooded.
Grove Street was flooded with water lapping up onto the hood of a police cruiser.
Lightning struck a tree, felling it onto a nearby house.
Lightning struck a house on Todd Road, setting it on fire.

The tornado touched down in Chelsea, where a window was blown out on Dudley Street. However, the overwhelming majority of damage occurred in Revere.  Most of the damage was rated EF-1, but EF-2 rated damage did occur near Revere Beach Parkway.  ||From Chelsea, the tornado moved across the Chelsea River, directly across the Paul Cronin Memorial Skating Rink.  Portions of the rink's roof were blown northeastward across Route 16.  Numerous houses on Revere Beach Parkway were damaged, with one roof blown completely off.  In that same area, large oak trees were snapped in half.  Numerous trees were downed, some of which were lifted up and then deposited on top of houses immediately behind Revere Beach Parkway.||The damage was widespread throughout much of the center of Revere.  The tornado traveled northward, following Route 107 or Broadway for the most part.  Windows were blown out of town hall and the roof was damaged.  A large birch tree was uprooted near town hall.  Sixty-four structures sustained damage that ranged from siding torn off to roofs lifted or blown off.  Thirteen of these structures (6 - 1 & 2 family homes, 3 - multifamily homes, and 4 commercial buildings) were deemed uninhabitable by building inspectors.  Several store signs were destroyed. Debris from homes collected on fences.  Trees fell on cars, a few of these crushed.||Revere High School also sustained damage, mainly to the exterior.  Side panels, fencing, sidewalks, and air handlers on the roof were damaged.||Police reported a car that had been overturned at the intersection of Revere Street and Carleton Avenue. Finally, near the rotary at Route 60 and Broadway, a billboard was blown onto several cars.||City officials estimated that city owned buildings alone sustained at least 1.5 to 2 million dollars of damage. ||While no major injuries were reported, several minor injuries occurred. An 86 year old woman suffered from a head laceration which she sustained from flying debris while standing outside a Dunkin Donuts.  A two week old baby girl strapped in the back seat of a truck was injured when a board flew through the rear windshield of the vehicle.  The board missed the infant but covered her in broken glass.
A microburst occurred in Needham resulting in numerous uprooted trees and downed power lines on Country Way and Moseley Avenue.
